title: Yankees, Rays fans guide with matchups, scouting reports, prediction
description: The New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays are playing a best-of-five American League Division Series.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Rays beat out the Yankees for first in the AL East and won more games than anyone in the league with one of the lowest payrolls playing an entertaining throwback style of aggressive baseball. They have three stars at the top of their lineup. They have a .300 hitter in the middle who can fly.

They bunt for hits, squeeze runners home and move runners better than anyone. Their rotation and bullpen are deep. Their record in one-run games was the best in the majors.

The Rays have the Yankees respect.

The Yankees also think they're the better team heading into a postseason showdown that seemed inevitable, a best-of-five Division Series between the two best teams in the league.

"At the end of the day, I think we played Tampa pretty well this year and I think we're in a good spot," Yankees ace Cam Schlittler said.

The Rays won the season series 7-6, but the Yankees feel they're peaking at the right time with their four aces finally all healthy at the same time.

They'll all be unleashed on the Rays. Gerrit Cole will start Saturday night's Game 1 at Tropicana Field, Schlittler will go Game 2, then the Yankees will go to their lefties when the series moves to New York with Carlos Rodon probably starting Game 3 and Max Fried pitching Game 4 if there's no sweep.

The Yankees' Division Series roster will be deeper than the 26-man squad that just swept the Red Sox in a Wild Card Series with 9-0 and 9-2 romps. Ryan Weathers is off the IL and available out of the bullpen, but Aaron Judge still isn't return to return from his Grade 2 calf strain.

The Yankees' one change from their their Wild Card Series roster was adding Weathers for an 11th pitcher and dropping infielder/outfielder Amed Rosario.

Second baseman Jazz Chisholm guaranteed the Yankees will win the series and Schlittler doubled down with "why would I disagree?"

The captain is also confident, regardless of his status.

"The Rays, they've got everything," Judge said. "It's a tough opponent. We're up in the task. We saw them all year. We had our battles, and we're just happy for the opportunity."

Here is a fans' guide to the Yankees-Rays Division Series with a look at how the teams match up and position-by-position scouting reports from an MLB scout:

Yankees: Luis Garcia Jr. (.277, 30 HR, 92 RBI, .831 OPS).

Rays: Jonathan Aranda (.274, 22 HR, 92 RBI, 792 OPS).

Scout's take: "Both teams have impact players at first base. I love Aranda, but the Yankees have held him down all season with their great pitching. If they do that in this series, the Yankees will be in real good shape. Garcia's had a great year. He's a free swinger who keeps getting better as a hitter. He capitalizes on mistakes in the zone."

Yankees: Jazz Chisholm (.231, 19 HR, 55 RBI).

Rays: Richie Palacios (.235, 10 HR, 57 RBI, .704) vs. RHP; Ben Williamson (.238, 3 HR, 26 RBI) vs. LHP.

Scout's take: "Jazz is playing for a contract and I think he badly wants to win a championship. He's motivated. Look at what he did against Boston. He didn't play against the lefty in Game 1, then he comes out in Game 2 and gets a couple hits with a walk. Tampa is going to be running out a bunch of righties at the Yankees this series, so Jazz will probably be in there and I can see him having a big series. Palacios and Williamson are ordinary role guys. That's all they are."

Yankees: George Lombard Jr. (.237, 7 HR, 22 RBI, .699 OPS).

Rays: Taylor Walls (.222, 2 HR, 36 RBI, 21 SB, .607 OPS).

Scout's take: "Lombard is 21 and he comes out against Boston hitting .500 with a home run in his first two playoff games. He was poised. He had good at-bats. Walls is one of the best defensive shortstops in baseball, but I don't like him one bit because this is a cocky guy who's never hit. If Walls played anywhere else, he would not be playing every day."

Yankees: Ryan McMahon (.213, 11 HR, 31 RBI, .635 OPS) & Jose Caballero (.231, 14 HR, 51 RBI, .655 OPS).

Rays: Junior Caminero (.276, 42 HR, 101 RBI, .885 OPS).

Scout's take: "Caminero is an emerging superstar. He's 23 with back-to-back 40-homer seasons. I don't see the Yankees letting Caminero beat them. Boone won't make the same mistake Boston did with Ben Rice in the Wild Card Series. Pitch around Caminero because he doesn't miss a pitch in the zone. You know what you're getting with McMahon when he's in there. He gives you good third-base play, but that's it."

Yankees: Heliot Ramos (.245, 13 HR, 46 RBI, .716 OPS).

Rays: Victor Mesa Jr. (.260, 14 HR, 34 RBI, .825 OPS).

Scout's take: "Ramos can hit left-handed pitching, but he'll be facing mostly righties in this series, so what kind of impact can he make? Mesa is fearless, he can hit the fastball and he's a solid defensive player."

Yankees: Spencer Jones (.245, 11 HR, 40 RBI, .742).

Rays: Cedric Mullins (.205, 15 HR, 48 RBI, .628) vs. RHP; Jonny DeLuca (.266, 11 HR, 50 RBI, 17 SB, .728 OPS vs. LHP.

Scout's take: "You have to put up with some punchouts with Jones, but he has a chance to hit it out of the ballpark and he plays decent defense. DeLuca is an underrated player with some pop, but I'm not a Mullins fan anymore. I used to be. Mullins doesn't run like he used to. He's a good outfielder, but not as good as he once was."

Yankees: Cody Bellinger (.264, 17 HR, 73 RBI, .768 OPS).

Rays: Chandler Simpson (.306, 0 HR, 38 RBI, 46 SB, .689 OPS).

Scout's take: "I like 'em both. Cody's the full package and I really like Simpson. Cody rose to the occasion against Boston. He knows he had to do more with Judge out, and he did. He's also the best defensive left fielder in the American League, maybe all of baseball. Simpson is contact oriented. He stays within himself. He doesn't try to hit the ball out of the ballpark and he's the fastest guy in the game. He's a good table setter. I'd take either of those guys on my team."

Yankees: Austin Wells (.187, 14 HR, 32 RBI, .624 OPS).

Rays: Liam Hicks (.284, 18 HR, 82 RBI, .801 OPS).

Scout's take: "Wells is riding a wave. He had the terrible first half, then he took a little time to get healthy. He was a different hitter in the second half and just had a heck of a Wild Card Series. He's become a pretty decent catcher. I remember watching Wells in the Fall League after he was drafted in the first round because of his bat. Well, he proved me wrong. He does a good job behind the plate. He's part of the reason why Yankees pitchers had the best ERA in baseball this year. The Rays getting Hicks from Miami added another big threat to a lineup that was very top heavy with Diaz, Aranda and Caminero hitting one, two, three. Hicks is a decent catch-and-throw receiver, too. This was a big get for Tampa because they've never had a catcher who can hit. Hicks brings a lot of offense. He's the full package."

Yankees: Ben Rice (.264, 41 HR, 97 RBI, .897).

Rays: Yandy Diaz (.293, 22 HR, 85 RBI, .825).

Scout's take: "Both of these guys are big-time game changers. Rice has more power, but Diaz is a better all-around hitter. You can tell Rice went to Dartmouth because he's a smart hitter. He looks for certain lanes. If the pitch isn't in that zone, he won't swing until he gets to two strikes. That's his kryptonite right there. I'd pitch around him every time he's up. Let Rice get himself out swinging at a bad pitch or walk him. Let somebody else beat you. If the other guys beat me, so be it. Diaz is a clutch hitter who has the ability to control the strike zone. This guy knows his game as a hitter. He has power, but he doesn't try to hit homers."

Yankees: LHP Carlos Rodon (7-3, 2.67); RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95); LHP Max Fried (5-5, 2.80); RHP Gerrit Cole (10-9, 3.61).

Rays: RHP Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67); RHP Freddy Peralta (10-11, 4.42); RHP Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10); LHP Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.21); RHP Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.53).

Scout's take: "Schlittler is the best pitcher in the league and all four of their starters can get into the seventh inning. How many teams can say that? Not many. That's a damn good playoff rotation. Shane McClanahan's injury really hurts Tampa. The Rays still have a bunch of No. 2 and No. 3 starters who can really pitch, but McClanahan is their big-game starter, their ace. He'd give them a left-hander to set the tone against a Yankees lineup that's usually filled with left-handed bats. This is a big loss for Tampa."

Yankees: RHP David Bednar (7-3, 2.47. 35 saves); RHP Paul Blackburn (7-3, 1.69); LHP Brent Headrick (7-4, 2.18); RHP John Schreiber (5-2, 3.28); RHP Will Warren (11-6, 3.92), LHP Ryan Weathers (5-8, 3.60); Ryan Yarbrough (2-1, 3.69).

Rays: RHP Bryan Baker (4-2, 1.44, 41 saves); LHP Garrett Cleavinger (4-4, 4.79); LHP Cam Booser (1-0, 1.98); RHP Kevin Kelly (6-4, 2.44); LHP Steven Matz (6-6, 5.39); RHP Cole Sulser (1-0, 4.31); RHP Tyler Wells (5-2, 2.38).

Scout's take: "There's a lot of good arms on both teams. I'm amazed what the Yankees are getting out of Blackburn. A couple of years ago, I had interest in him for my team, then I fell out of favor when his velo dropped. Now Blackburn is overpowering. A key for the Rays will be their lefties. They don't have anyone like Headrick, but you better believe they'll use all of them this series to try neutralizing all those left-handed hitters in the Yankees lineup. Booser has been effective, but he's more of a touch-and-feel guy. He's not going to strike Ben Rice out in a big spot. Another thing, all of Tampa's left-handed relievers are prone to mistakes left over the plate, especially Matz. If they do that, Tampa's in trouble."

Yankees: Paul Goldschmidt (.252, 18 HR, 52 RBI); CF Trent Grisham (.211, 18 HR, 59 RBI); C Ali Sanchez (.244, 1 HR, 8 RBI, .577 OPS), Anthony Volpe (.245, 3 HR, 28 RBI, .658 OPS).

Rays: C Nick Fortes (.258, 6 HR, 35 RBI); INF Jorge Mateo (.203, 5 HR, 18 RBI, 19 SB, 559 OPS); INF/OF Ryan Vilade (.245, 11 HR, 45 RBI, .750 OPS); 2B Richie Palacios/Ben Williamson; OF Cedric Mullins/ Jonny DeLuca.

Scout's take: "The Yankees have power, athleticism and some guys who can play different positions on their bench. Aaron Boone will be able to force Kevin Cash into some moves that he really doesn't want to make because the Yankees have more of a surplus off the bench."

Yankees: Aaron Boone (970-575; 8 playoff berths, 1 pennant, 9th season).

Rays: Kevin Cash, (994-848, 6 playoff berths, 1 pennant, 12th season).

Scout's take: "I've been a big Aaron Boone fan since he was in college at USC. I liked his game and his makeup. He's become a really good manager in a big market to the point where I think Brian Cashman isn't forcing the Yankees to live and die over analytics. From the games I've watched, I think Boone has more leeway to manage with his head than he did in past seasons. He does a great job year after year getting teams loaded with injuries into the playoffs and usually winning series. I like Cash, too. I like that he bunts a lot. Tampa has to play that way because they don't have the power that the Yankees and a lot of other clubs do. I think there's some micromanaging there with Cash because of all this inundated analytics BS that Tampa does. It works for them, but they have not brought home a world championship."

title: The Wildcats suffer a blowout in New Jersey
description: The ‘Cats were outplayed on Friday night.
fullText:
The Wildcats faced Rutgers (5-4-1, 3-1) in New Jersey on Friday night and lost 4-0, bringing the conference record down to .500, although the 'Cats will stay in the top half of the Big Ten standings despite the loss.

The Scarlett Knights came out swinging at the start of the game, scoring three goals in the first ten minutes after a lackluster early defensive performance. First, sophomore Pius Ssebulime netted a beautiful header into the bottom right corner in the third minute.

Just six minutes later, junior Dan Karsten scored a loose ball in the goalie box to give the Scarlett Knights a two-goal lead. Northwestern head coach Russell Payne challenged the call, looking for a handball, but despite a lengthy VAR check, the refs disagreed.

With 8:22 elapsed from the clock, the Wildcats got their first shot of the night off a set piece into the box. Rutgers grad student Rafael Ponce de Leon made the save. Four passes and fifteen seconds later, Rutgers got the ball to grad student Amer Lukovic at the top of the box. He slotted it in, giving the Knights a 3-0 lead.

The Wildcats held the line for the rest of the half, allowing just one shot on goal, while putting up zero themselves.

The second half was a defensive clinic from both teams, with no shots on goal by either side for the first 23 minutes. In the 69th minute of play, Northwestern Junior Gabriel Smyth put a shot on target from outside of the box to the top right corner, forcing a stellar jumping save from Ponce de Leon.

Two minutes later, Lukovic dribbled into the right side of the box and pushed one past the Northwestern goalkeeper to score his second goal of the night and cap off the 4-0 lead.

Northwestern won both the corners battle and the shots battle 11-7 and 14-13, respectively, but neither stat helped the offense generate quality chances, and they finished with just three shots on goal and a clean sheet for their opponents.

Northwestern gets a week off before facing their biggest travel day of the year when they go west to face Washington. That game is on October 10th at 9 pm CT and streaming on Big+.

fullText:
Last-minute fantasy football streaming options for Week 4 2026: Tight End appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Tight ends can rapidly frustrate fantasy managers more than almost any other position, especially once the clear weekly starters are no longer available. This often leads to tough decisions, such as choosing between projecting four or five targets versus hoping a player scores a touchdown. Week 4 offers a better selection of waiver-wire options than usual, with several widely available players entering Sunday with either an established receiving role, a significant increase in usage, or a favorable matchup that could create new opportunities not seen in the first month.

This week presents three distinct streaming profiles. Juwan Johnson, who is rostered in 55% of leagues, has emerged as one of the most productive players at his position. Kenyon Sadiq remains available in about two-thirds of leagues, despite a breakout performance. Meanwhile, Brenton Strange is only rostered in 18% of leagues ahead of a matchup against a Cincinnati defense that has been particularly vulnerable to tight ends. NFL.com's Week 4 waiver-wire analysis highlighted all three as top additions at the position.

Ultimately, the decision depends on what a fantasy lineup needs most. Managers who are protecting a projected lead can focus on reliable targets, while those chasing a higher upside may want to consider younger players whose roles are evolving quickly. For deeper leagues, matchup hunting provides another approach, especially where the most obvious waiver options have already been claimed.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Johnson is no longer just a temporary solution based on one favorable performance. His production has remained consistent through the first three games, and Week 3 provided clear evidence that his role has grown substantial enough to offer weekly fantasy value, rather than being merely touchdown-dependent.

In his latest appearance, the veteran caught eight passes for 53 yards and two touchdowns, totaling 23.3 fantasy points. More importantly, these receptions highlight what fantasy managers should focus on when assessing performance beyond just the final score. While two touchdowns might vanish the following week, eight catches indicate consistent involvement in the offense, thus providing a much stronger foundation for his production. After three weeks, he ranked third among fantasy tight ends, making it particularly surprising that he remains available in nearly half of ESPN leagues.

Atlanta will be visiting New Orleans on Monday night, giving the Saints another chance to utilize their short-area passing game and the middle of the field, which has already created such a valuable role, and while divisional familiarity can sometimes limit explosive plays, it can benefit a tight end who does not rely on deep targets to score points.

The main appeal is that fantasy managers don't need another two-touchdown performance to justify starting him. Even five or six catches with moderate yardage can provide a respectable floor in a position where many alternatives struggle with only a few targets and hope for luck near the goal line. Should another red-zone opportunity come along, his ceiling could increase quickly without requiring an unusual uptick in targets, as continuity also has value. New Orleans has already demonstrated that this part of the offense is effective, so there is little reason to significantly reduce the involvement of a reliable intermediate target after three productive weeks. This makes him the safest streaming option available, assuming he is still on the waiver wire.

Sadiq is an exciting player to consider because Week 3 may have marked the moment his role shifted from being a developmental rookie to a legitimate fantasy option. He caught seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown against Detroit, showcasing far more than just a one-time breakout, and the eight targets are significant because they indicate that New York consistently trusted him within the passing game. His 105 yards show that these opportunities weren't limited to short checkdowns near the line of scrimmage.

NFL.com ranked him as the second-best tight end waiver target heading into Week 4, noting that he is still rostered in only 34% of ESPN leagues. His first-round pedigree is important, as his athletic potential was never in doubt, and the uncertainty was mainly about how quickly he would gain enough responsibility to be valuable in fantasy, especially considering the position requires players to juggle receiving concepts, blocking assignments, and protection responsibilities simultaneously.

Chicago provides Sadiq the chance to prove that his increased involvement was more than a one-game anomaly because New York doesn't need another triple-digit receiving performance for him to be a worthwhile option, as even five targets would be enough opportunity for his athleticism to generate a useful fantasy line, especially if one of those opportunities comes in the red zone.

Naturally, this option carries more risk than a veteran player in New Orleans. One breakout performance doesn't guarantee that eight targets will become the norm, and young pass catchers can experience sudden fluctuations in volume due to changing offensive game plans. Fantasy managers should view Week 3's production as evidence of increasing potential rather than a newfound guaranteed level of performance.

Strange enters Week 4 in a unique situation because his appeal has less to do with a sudden surge in statistics and more to do with the defense that Jacksonville will face.

Cincinnati has struggled significantly against tight ends during the first month of the season. In Week 3 alone, tight ends amassed 97 receiving yards against their defense on just five receptions, and although Strange has been relatively quiet with limited opportunities so far, NFL.com identified him as one of the top streaming options for the week due to this favorable matchup. With an 18% roster rate, he is attainable in nearly every league.

The Bengals have allowed enough production over the middle to present a realistic opportunity for useful yardage, even without a high number of targets. Four or five opportunities can be enough when a defense is giving up significant gains at the position, especially if Jacksonville reaches the red zone and creates scoring opportunities.

However, the risk is evident because the floor is lower compared to other options, as modest volume can vanish quickly if the matchup doesn't unfold as anticipated. For example, a three-target game without a touchdown could leave fantasy managers wanting for help elsewhere in their lineup, making this stream less secure for teams seeking stability.

For deeper leagues, though, this uncertainty brings a clear advantage: availability. Managers who missed out on earlier waiver wire opportunities can still find a player in a matchup that is particularly favorable for his position, without relying on injuries elsewhere to create more playing time.

Week 4 presents enough variety that fantasy managers should not treat every waiver option the same way, and there are multiple paths to success: consistent receiving involvement, the emergence of a rookie in a key role, or the advantage of an exploitable matchup can all provide value, even if a player isn't likely to have a standout season.

The best strategy is to align these player profiles with the needs of your roster, rather than simply pursuing whoever posted the highest statistics from the previous Sunday. Tight end remains a volatile position outside of the elite tier, but by understanding where target opportunities and favorable coverage situations are likely to arise, you can manage that volatility more effectively.

fullText:
Phillies rumors: Ken Rosenthal urges Bryce Harper or Kyle Schwarber trade, but there are 'tricky' problems appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Philadelphia Phillies were recently eliminated from the Major League Baseball Playoffs by the Atlanta Braves. Heading into the 2027 season, Philadelphia is getting some advice from MLB insider Ken Rosenthal. Rosenthal thinks the team should trade either Bryce Harper or Kyle Schwarber.

"The Phillies at least need to kick around the idea of trading one of them. Actually following through, though, would be another matter, given (John) Middleton's affection for both players," Rosenthal wrote for The Athletic.

Rosenthal predicts problems if the Phillies try to trade one of these players.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Besides, trading Harper or Schwarber would be tricky," Rosenthal wrote. "Harper declined opt outs in the 13-year, $330 million free-agent deal he signed with the Phillies prior to the 2019 season. He no longer wished to be the subject of trade rumors. He wanted to settle in one city for the rest of his career."

There are other issues that involve Schwarber.

"Interested teams could view Harper as either a first baseman or right fielder. Schwarber, who is strictly a designated hitter, does not offer that kind of defensive utility. And the Phillies would be reluctant to move a player who is the team's heart and soul and leads the majors with 232 home runs the past five seasons," Rosenthal wrote.

Philadelphia has been one of the strongest teams in the National League over the last few years. The Phillies though have struggled in the MLB Playoffs. Their last World Series title was in 2008, although the club made the World Series in 2009 and 2022.

The Phillies started the 2026 season with a tough stretch. Following a bad losing streak near the start of the year, the franchise fired former manager Rob Thomson. Thomson was replaced by Don Mattingly, who turned around the club.

Mattingly is expected not to return as manager in 2027. Philadelphia has long been linked with Alex Cora, who was fired as manager of the Boston Red Sox during the 2026 season.

title: Lazio 3-3 Juve Stabia: Entertaining Friendly at Formello
description: At the Formello Training Centre, Lazio played their second friendly of the extended international break, hosting Serie B boys Juve Stabia.Absent Lazio PlayersLazio entered the game without the eight p...
fullText:
At the Formello Training Centre, Lazio played their second friendly of the extended international break, hosting Serie B boys Juve Stabia.

Lazio entered the game without the eight players who were called up for international duty: Christos Mandas, Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen, Josip Sutalo, Kenneth Taylor, Davide Frattesi, Nuno Tavares, and Albert Gudmundsson, who returned early after dislocating his shoulder.

The Iceland star joined Nicolo Rovella, Adam Marusic, Danilo Cataldi, Adrian Przyborek, and Bruno Galassi on the sidelines, while Fisayo Dele-Bashiru made his return to the squad.

Gennaro Gattuso once again tested a 4-2-3-1 formation while keeping the same lineup that played against Arezzo last weekend. Edoardo Motta started in goal behind Romano Floriani Mussolini, Danilho Doekhi, Diogo Leite, and Alfonso Pedraza.

In midfield, Valerio Farcomeni joined Reda Belahyane in the double pivot. Club captain Mattia Zaccagni started on the left wing, with the young Federico Serra on the opposite flank, while Andrea Pinamonti led the line, with Tijjani Noslin behind him.

While the Biancocelesti held possession, they created few chances in the first 30 minutes. They eventually managed to break the deadlock at the half-hour mark when Pinamonti picked up a loose ball following a scramble inside the box and found Farcomeni on the left side. The young midfielder teed up Noslin with a perfect cross, and the Dutchman's header sailed into the far corner.

However, Lazio's lead was short-lived, as Juve Stabia levelled the score less than two minutes later from a corner kick that found no one in particular, but David Buglio was the quickest to react, slotting it past Motta from close range.

In the 39th minute, Lazio retook the lead thanks to Zaccagni. The hosts' pressing paid off, as Pedraza collected a poor pass, skipped past his marker and trotted towards the byline before feeding his captain with a back-pass. The winger's first-time attempt took a small deflection, but it was enough to upset the goalkeeper.

But once again, the Aquile failed to maintain their advantage for more than a few minutes. Fabio Maistro received the ball on the edge of the penalty box, and he found the bottom corner with a delicate shot that beat Motta.

After the break, Lazio had an inviting opportunity to lead for the third time. Juve Stabia's Substitute goalkeeper Pietro Boer played a poor pass that was intercepted by Noslin. The Lazio striker was brought down by Thomas Battistella inside the box. However, the goalkeeper was able to atone by pulling out a solid save on Pinamonti.

In the 65th minute, the visitors took the lead for the first time, as Lazio were punished by none other than their own player, Sana Fernandes. The loaned-out winger controlled a long ball expertly before prevailing in his duel against Manuel Lazzari. Finally, he chipped it past Motta before apologising to his parent club.

After wasting a penalty, Pinamonti was able to get on the scoresheet in the 78th minute. Boer committed another blunder, as he was caught napping on the ball outside his penalty box, allowing Noslin to pick his pocket. The ball reached the Italian striker, who easily directed it towards the empty net.

The Biancocelesti had several chances to find a winner, but the result remained unchanged. Gattuso will welcome back his international players next week before resuming the Serie A campaign with a home fixture against Monza on October 11.

description: HENRICO, VA. Grimsley’s marching band was asked to leave and escorted out of the stadium […]
fullText:
HENRICO, VA. (WGHP) – Even though Grimsley Senior High School's football team came away with a huge out-of-conference road win, a 24-17 victory over Varina in Henrico, Va., on Friday, not all Whirlies fans were celebrating at the end of the game.

Grimsley's marching band was asked to leave and escorted out of the stadium during the second half after the public address announcer repeatedly warned both bands not to play music while the ball was in play.

Victim taken to hospital after shooting on Pichard Street in Greensboro

According to an affiliate with the Grimsley band, who wished to remain anonymous, the Varina marching band was playing while the ball was in play during the first half of the game.

At halftime, Grimsley's band leadership consulted with the head referee, who told them he would not penalize either band for playing while the ball was in play.

According to the Grimsley source, after playing music while the ball was in play twice in the second half, the public address announcer warned both bands again. Varina's band was not playing at the time since they were on a break after the halftime show.

Grimsley ignored these requests and kept playing while the ball was in play, which led to Varina officials ejecting the Grimsley band from the stadium with a police escort.

FOX8 reached out to Varina and Grimsley High School officials for comment, but has not received a response.

title: ‘Should have stayed retired’ – Radio host makes fun of Aaron Donald’s start to the season with the LA Rams
description: Aaron Donald’s return to the NFL has been underwhelming not just for him as a player, but also for his team, the Los Angeles Rams. They are currently third in the NFC West with a 1-2 record and will be up against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, October 3.
fullText:
Aaron Donald's return to the NFL has been underwhelming not just for him as a player, but also for his team, the Los Angeles Rams.

They are currently third in the NFC West with a 1-2 record and will be up against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, October 3. However, they will be playing this game without their franchise legend Aaron Donald, who has been ruled out due to a back injury.

Head coach Sean McVay in his press conference confirmed that the player was doing well, but the team did not want to take any chances.

In two games so far, the three-time Defensive Player of the Year has not had the best of statistical output, and with the Rams losing against the Denver Broncos, criticism has started to mount on Donald.

When the Rams announced the return of Donald, many analysts named them as favourites to win the Super Bowl. He was out for the game in Australia, but returned to the line-up for their second game against the New York Giants. He looked good in that game, but was not at his best in the 30-26 loss to the Broncos.

"He's been Casper the friendly ghost, how can you be that big and be that invisible… He's had no pressures. He's like 79th out of 91 guys rushing the passer, what is going on?" said Rob Parker on Fox's The Odd Couple podcast.

"He's been a zero since he came back and now he got a back issue. He should have stayed retired, I tried to tell you this."

In the two games Donald played, he had a pressure rate of 4.8%, which ranks 79th out of 91 NFL players. This indicates that he has not started the season well, but considering he has returned after a two-year absence, some rust was expected. However, what is hurting the Rams is that they also do not have Myles Garrett, who is ruled out for 4-6 weeks due to injury.

Donald will be hoping that he finds form soon, as he returned to help the Rams get to the Super Bowl. Currently, they look far from a team that can play in February, but if Donald gets back to his former self and Garrett returns to fitness, the Rams could be the team that many believed during preseason.

title: Welcome to the New Era
description: Northwestern is a football school.
fullText:
There are no words that can describe the atmosphere. You had to be there.

Northwestern just made a statement to the college football world that Evanston is home to a football school.

That student section. In-freaking-sane. From the moment Penn State's special teams came out to warm up, the noise began.

And that entrance. Of all the famously known college football entrances, this one is for sure up there. Hell's Bells into Thunderstruck with a live guitarist was just beautiful.

From the moment the players ran the length of the field, they immediately began hyping up the Wildcat Wall. The standing-only student section proved to be worth it, and the players got really into it.

Caleb Komolafe said postgame that celebrating with the student section was the most memorable part of the game, and it wrapped up as a night to remember. And don't get me started on Don't Stop Believin'. Northwestern may have its Jump Around or Mr. Brightside. Everything was executed to perfection to cap off a dominant win.

Speaking of execution, Northwestern ran for 414 yards, the most in a game for the Wildcats since 2003. Komolafe and Joseph Himon II each rushed for over 150 yards and broke off explosive play after explosive play. Aidan Chiles threw the ball just 14 times, but he didn't need to do that much with the rushing attack playing at this level. Northwestern's offensive line played a huge role, so much so that Chiles said, "I'm going to take them out to eat for sure."

Even with injuries galore, including being down Luke Dehnicke, Damon Walters, Braden Turner and Josh Fussell, who was seen on crutches and with a boot on his right foot postgame, the Wildcats dominated in their stadium opener.

Northwestern's defense also got in on the action, limiting Penn State to 291 total yards, 13 points and picking off Rocco Becht twice. Last week, Northwestern rushed for just 53 yards and allowed 271. Penn State rushed for only 48 in this game and were outgained by a full year (365 yards). I'm really excited to watch the film on this one to dive deeper into what worked so well for the 'Cats' rushing attack.

I still have chills from being at that game, and that stretches beyond being an InsideNU writer. It was different. It was special. This stadium will revolutionize the sport, and Northwestern won't "sound like a library" going forward.

Welcome to the new era of Northwestern football. As coach Braun said, "Why not us?"

title: 'Best midfielder in the world': Liverpool star told he's as good as Zidane
description: Liverpool have not had an overly easy time of it, results-wise, at the start of the 2026/27 season. Andoni Iraola has presided over only two victories in his opening five Premier League games - agains...
fullText:
Liverpool have not had an overly easy time of it, results-wise, at the start of the 2026/27 season.

Andoni Iraola has presided over only two victories in his opening five Premier League games - against newly promoted Ipswich Town as well as former club Bournemouth.

It is going to take a while for the Basque tactico's ideas to come across but there's no doubt we've seen promising signs already.

Alexander Isak for example is back among the goals on a more regular basis while improvements have been made to the backline too.

Liverpool are possessed of world-class talent in the midfield meanwhile - and it's only a matter of time before the Anfield side start firing on all cylinders.

The club offered new contracts to both Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai over the past few months.

Szoboszlai, 25, has hit the ground running for club AND country this season - hitting an unbelievable goal in the EFL Cup victory over Tottenham.

The Hungarian captain has carried on that fine form during the international window - excelling in the weekend win against Giorgi Mamardashvili's Georgia where Milos Kerkez scored the only goal of the game.

Szoboszlai's performance was so good in the heart of midfield that Georgian coach Giorgi Tsetsadze - in charge of top-flight side Rustavi - told Hungarian media that the Liverpool man reminded him of a certain Zinedine Zidane on the night.

"Looking at Dominik Szoboszlai, I thought of Zinédine Zidane – and not because of his hair…" he tells Nemzeti Sport.

"Seriously, his performance was almost perfect both in attack and defense.

"He was constantly looking for opportunities to pass forward, he was rushing towards the goal, trying to score, and what is especially important, he not only played forward in the middle of the field, but also gave dangerous passes in the final third.

"I think he is one of the best midfielders in the world at the moment."

Zidane is one of a select band of players to win the UEFA Champions League, the FIFA World Cup as well as the Ballon d'Or and goes down as one of the all-time greats of the game.

Iraola will be hoping to tap into those Zizou-like traits on a more regular basis once Szoboszlai returns from international duty.

description: Four playoff games stacked back to back as the MLB playoffs continue in earnest!
fullText:
The Baseball Gods have lined up over 10 consecuive hours of baseball for you to view this Saturday as both the National League and American League Division Series begin.

Heat's Giannis is thrilled he doesn't have to play against Bam Adebayo anymore appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

During his tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks, Giannis Antetokounmpo has spent years dealing with Bam Adebayo as an opponent. Now, with the Miami Heat, the Greek Freak will finally be on the same side.

Antetokounmpo recently spoke about his new teammate and admitted he is glad he no longer has to face Adebayo on the court.

"Playing against Bam, it was hard. I'm happy I don't have to deal with that anymore," Antetokounmpo said.

"Playing against Bam, it was hard. I'm happy I don't have to deal with that anymore, and other players have to."

Giannis Antetokounmpo is relieved that Bam Adebayo is no longer his matchup 😅

(via @espn)pic.twitter.com/rHOC1l8JuC

— ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 3, 2026

Coming this NBA season, Antetokounmpo will be adjusting to his new surroundings after spending the first 13 years of his NBA career with the Bucks. He joined Miami this offseason and will now team up with Adebayo as the Heat prepare for the 2026-27 season.

Antetokounmpo also praised Adebayo's approach as a leader and teammate.

"He's a great leader, vocal, but, most importantly, he's going to lead by example," Antetokounmpo said. "He's never going to have us do something that he's not going to do himself."

The pairing is set to give Miami two elite athletes who can impact the game in different ways. Adebayo can create from the frontcourt, while Antetokounmpo remains one of the league's most dangerous players attacking the basket and in transition.

There will still be an adjustment period. Antetokounmpo acknowledged that Miami's spacing and player movement are different from what he experienced in Milwaukee.

He described a training camp possession in which he threw a pass expecting a teammate to be in one spot, only for the player to move elsewhere.

Miami will spend the preseason working through those details. For Antetokounmpo, though, at least he no longer has to figure out how to get past Adebayo.

title: Report Shows Why NY Giants & Lions Avoided Big Mistake By Losing Joey Porter Jr. Trade Sweepstakes
description: While some New York Giants and Detroit Lions fans hoped their teams made a trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey […]
fullText:
While some New York Giants and Detroit Lions fans hoped their teams made a trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., it looks like they avoided a big mistake, based on opinions from around the NFL.

The Steelers have had to deal with the Porter Jr. cloud hanging over the team for months, as the disgruntled three-year veteran apparently faked a back injury until the team gave him the contract extension he wanted or traded him.

Well, the latter came this week when the Steelers sent the corner to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder. Following the trade, fans from teams that didn't get the talented CB wondered why their teams couldn't pull the trigger on a similar deal.

However, there are "many around" the NFL who feel that it was a good decision by teams like the Giants and Lions. "Many around the league believed Dallas overpaid, based largely on the belief that teams don't view Porter as a top-tier corner," The Athletic's Jonathan Jones claims.

There is no doubt that Porter Jr. would have made the Giants' and Lions secondary better. Especially since both teams need help in their secondaries right now. He is one of the better corners in the AFC, and you can never have enough reliable play in that part of the defense.

However, the 26-year-old has never earned year-end Pro Bowl and All-Pro honors. But he wants to be paid like an elite cornerback in his next contract. Something the team that knows him better than anyone- the Steelers- balked at. It is one thing to give up a lot of money. It is another to give up valuable picks and money for a player that isn't a Pro Bowler (yet).

Jones notes that the 2027 NFL Draft class is projected to be very good. So that means a sixth-rounder next year is better than most years. In 2028, the Steelers will get a second-round pick. That is a spot in the draft where franchises can land high-level talent. It is why many around the NFL believe the Cowboys once again overpaid in a trade, especially since they still need to re-sign him.

title: New York Liberty face the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals
description: — Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons.New York will be making its third appearance in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs in the past four years when the Liberty play the Atlanta Dream on Sunday in Game 1 of the best-of-five series.
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons.

New York will be making its third appearance in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs in the past four years when the Liberty play the Atlanta Dream on Sunday in Game 1 of the best-of-five series.

"Experience in the playoffs definitely matters," Stewart said Friday before practice. "There's so many things (during a longer series) that you have to stay focused on the end goal."

That end goal would be reaching the WNBA Finals and trying to win a second title in three seasons.

"With this group, for the majority of us, (we've) been in this type of series, where it's not getting too high or too low is the huge important part," Stewart said. "And what we did in the first round is great — we're happy to be here — but that wasn't a goal for our season to get out of the first round."

New York was dominant in the first round while sweeping the Minnesota Lynx, becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the league's 30-year history.

"The approach that we're having in these playoffs is pretty much where you want to be," Stewart added. "We're the ones that are staying poised, staying under control at all times. But we're gonna be aggressive for the full 40 minutes, and if you want something, you're gonna have to go through us to get it."

Atlanta is the newcomer to this round, advancing this far for the first time since 2018. Aware of the team's lack of playoff experience other than Jordin Canada, Dream GM Dan Padover went out and got DeWanna Bonner as a free agent in late August. Bonner has played 100 games in the playoffs, the most in league history.

She joined a stacked lineup that includes Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray and Angel Reese. That group lifted the Dream to their first playoff win since 2016 when they swept the Washington Mystics.

"I think the pace that they were playing with was really good," Liberty coach Chris DeMarco said. "I think (Bonner) brought a lot of veteran leadership to them, a lot of timely scoring to really settle them into games. I think Howard and Gray are just two really good — or great guards that we have to slow down. When the game gets tough, they kind of put their heads down and kind of take over that scoring."

The Atlanta Dream had one of the best defenses in the league this year, anchored by the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese. Atlanta led the league in steals per game (9.1), which it converted to 18.1 points per game. The Dream raised that in the playoffs, scoring 27 points off miscues in their Game 1 win over Washington and getting 23 

They are very active getting into passing lanes, which makes scoring in transition difficult.

The two teams met in the final two games of the regular season with the No. 4 seed on the line, and the Dream won both those contests. Stewart sat out the second game to get some rest heading into the playoffs. Neither team puts much stock in the value of those two games, other than they provided fresh film to both sides from late in the season.

The Dream will play the first two games of the semifinals in State Farm Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks. Atlanta played six regular-season games at the arena, which seats more than 17,000 fans. The Dream's usual home, the Gateway Center Arena, holds about 3,500. Atlanta played Game 1 of its series against the Mystics at State Farm Arena. If the Dream win in the semifinals, it's unclear what they'll do for the Finals since singer Sombr is performing there the night of Game 3 and the Hawks have their home opener the same evening as Game 4.

title: WATCH: Saints produce must-see hype video for Week 4 vs. Falcons
description: The New Orleans Saints produced a must-see hype video narrated by Curtis Deloatch and Steve Gleason for Monday night's game with the Atlanta Falcons.
fullText:
You've got to see this. The New Orleans Saints produced a must-see hype video for Monday night's game with the Atlanta Falcons -- narrated by Saints legends Curtis Deloatch and Steve Gleason. Gleason, of course, blocked an early punt against the Falcons twenty years ago in the "Rebirth" game that New Orleans is celebrating. It was Deloatch who recovered that blocked punt and returned it for a touchdown, lighting up the home crowd and powering the Saints to a 23-3 win.

"I can still close my eyes and hear that crowd. That day, you could feel it in your soul, man," Deloatch began.

That victorious return to the Superdome, the first home game played in New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina flooded the city and devastated the region, remains one of the most emotional moments in NFL history. It was a cathartic experience for people who had lost so much and spent a year trying to piece themselves back together. Seeing their team get a win in prime time proved to be a light at the end of that long dark tunnel. The decades since have been filled with the winnginest years Saints fans have ever seen.

"Let's stamp a new page into the history books," Gleason added, using the innovative text-to-speech generator that's given him a voice during his lifelong battle with ALS.

Twenty years ago, the world heard New Orleans roar again.

Same Dome. Same Rival. Same Monday night stage.

Let them hear us again ⚜️#Saints | @nutrl_usa pic.twitter.com/NzVTY7kEaO

fullText:
The state, which is home to many AI companies, is one of the first to roll out workplace regulations targeting the technology

California’s laws aimed at protecting workers from the impacts of artificial intelligence could pave the way for broader workplace safeguards across the US as calls for regulating the technology mount. As the federal government goes hands-off on AI, California is taking the reins to address workers’ biggest fears.

The new laws come as workers increasingly worry whether AI will take their jobs, lead to discrimination and increase workplace surveillance. Unions, worker advocates and even some lawmakers pushed for the new rules, a regulatory shift for a technology that has largely developed unchecked. California, home to many of the leading companies developing AI, represents one of the first states to roll out a sweeping set of workplace regulations targeting the technology.

“It’s a turning point,” said Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO, who’s been helping leaders across the country write regulations. “It’s really the first time we’re seeing California workers showing the country that we don’t have to accept [this].”

Other states that have recently passed individual laws aimed at AI’s use in the workplace include Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois and Texas, narrower in scope than California’s. And more bills across the county are being lined up for consideration, Gonzalez said.

California’s laws aim to target workplace surveillance measures like heat maps that track employees’ movements, including how long they spend in the bathroom, or having their emotional states monitored. Amazon warehouse workers have previously complained about being timed on their bathroom breaks, for example. And at Kaiser Permanente, nurses have said automated systems rated their tone of voice in patient interactions.

But the laws could also prevent future unexpected harms.

“We don’t know all the places companies are using AI, and that is and should be scary,” Gonzalez said.

Part of the strategy for worker advocates and union groups like the California Federation has been following AI companies’ latest products. “If it’s being sold, that’s a good indication” it could be in use, Gonzales said. The federation also plans to use the momentum to revive issues like requiring employers to disclose when they’re using AI in the workplace, which was a bill that died in the state’s assembly appropriations committee this year.

California’s new laws are a key step in gaining regulatory ground for worker advocates, said Robin Feldman, director and founder of AI Law & Innovation Institute at The University of California College of the Law, San Francisco. Still, the statutes are somewhat limited in how they are implemented.

“The bills have no private enforcement,” Feldman said. “In other words: workers can’t sue. Only the government can enforce the laws.”

The new regulations come amid a backdrop of record AI spending at big tech companies along with massive job cuts. But workers have started pushing back. In June, Meta paused a program that tracked workers’ computer activities to train its AI models. And one month later, dozens of employees filed a lawsuit claiming the tech company’s AI tools targeted those with disability accommodations or on medical or parental leaves for layoffs.

Meanwhile, safety concerns, including fears that AI could destroy humanity, have been garnering more attention from lawmakers across the country and prompted OpenAI and Anthropic to call for slowing the pace of development.

“Workers are increasingly part of that movement, speaking up about the fear of job loss and the dehumanizing experience of being surveilled and controlled by an algorithm,” said Annette Bernhardt, senior tech policy adviser at UC Berkeley Labor Center.

While the new laws “have teeth”, according to Danielle Ochs, shareholder at employment law firm Ogletree Deakins’ San Francisco office, it’s unclear how sweeping the change will be. Ochs said employers generally aren’t grappling with the AI uses outlined in the new regulations and instead are more interested in how to responsibly implement AI across their systems.

“Having 10 hoops you have to jump through per tool is not reflective of reality,” she said. It would be better to have “guardrails that are more aligned” with employers’ wider use of AI rather than focused on specific tools or uses.

She says opponents worry that the new rules could unexpectedly prohibit helpful AI that might, for example, ensure truckers don’t fall asleep at the wheel.

While it’s too soon to gauge how effective the laws will be, worker advocates believe the momentum is moving in a positive direction. Gonzalez said the measures are only the beginning of addressing AI’s potential impacts.

“We have so much work to do,” she said. “But this should give us all hope we can win … against the tech lobby, against big corporations, because we are the majority.”

title: OpenXW, a modern enhanced port of Star Wars: X-Wing
description: Contribute to elyosh/OpenXW development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
OpenXW is an open-source reimplementation of Star Wars: X-Wing for
Windows, macOS, and Linux. It runs the original game data natively on current
systems and supports both the 1994 Collector's CD-ROM and the 1998 Windows
release.

With both editions installed, OpenXW can combine the 1994 menus, cutscenes,
and adaptive iMUSE soundtrack with the 1998 flight simulation and 3D assets.

OpenXW does not include any content from the original game. A complete
installation of at least one supported edition is required. Install both
editions to use the recommended combination.

Star Wars: X-Wing Special Edition is available from
GOG and
Steam.

The 1994 and 1998 releases each have their own presentation, flight simulation,
and soundtrack. OpenXW lets the menus and cutscenes, flight simulation, and
music be selected independently.

The recommended configuration combines:

This retains the 1998 flight presentation without giving up the interactive
music of the Collector's CD-ROM. Either supported edition can also be played
on its own.

The original 1993 flight graphics and missions are also available with an
extracted 1993 installation including the B-Wing expansion. This mode uses
the menus and cutscenes from an installed 1994 or 1998 edition.

OpenXW reimplements the adaptive iMUSE soundtrack from the 1994 Collector's
CD-ROM. The music responds to mission events and moves seamlessly between
themes during flight.

OpenXW can emulate Roland MT-32 and SC-55 Sound Canvas synthesizers. These
require compatible ROMs supplied by the user.

Built-in AdLib and OPL3 emulation are available for the classic FM-synth sound,
while FluidSynth can play the General MIDI soundtrack with a user-selected
SoundFont.

The original prerecorded 1998 music remains available when the complete 1998
experience is preferred.

OpenXW offers classic and modern graphics modes. Classic mode preserves the
original game's appearance, while modern mode combines the original models
and cockpit artwork with high-resolution rendering.

With the 1998 flight graphics, modern enhancements include:

The DOS flight graphics can also be rendered at higher resolutions with MSAA,
preserving their original untextured models.

Press TAB during flight to switch between classic and modern graphics.

Unlocked flight timing provides smoother motion and more responsive input on
modern displays. Native timing remains available in settings when the original
flight timing is preferred.

Flight can be played with a mouse and keyboard, gamepad, or joystick. Mouse
flight offers both classic controls and a virtual stick, with adjustable
sensitivity and Y-axis inversion. Modern gamepads and joysticks are supported,
with configurable axes, deadzones, and button bindings.

OpenXW validates the selected installations and remembers them for future
launches.

Press ESC to open OpenXW Settings. The Mouse tab lets you choose
between classic and virtual-stick mouse flight controls.

OpenXW remains under active development. Bugs and differences from the
original releases are still possible.

Fans of Totally Games' space simulators may also be interested in
OpenTIE, an open-source reimplementation
of Star Wars: TIE Fighter,
OpenXvT, an open-source reimplementation
of Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter with Balance of Power, and
OpenXWA, an open-source reimplementation
of Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance. All run on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Join the TotallyOpen Discord server to discuss
OpenXW, OpenTIE, OpenXvT, OpenXWA, development, and the Totally Games flight
simulators.

Release packages include the required runtime libraries. Keep the executable,
libraries, resources, and shader directories together when moving an
installation. Linux also requires the system GLib and GThread libraries.

title: The Essence of Software
description: home
fullText:
As our dependence on technology increases, the design of software matters more than ever before. Why then is so much software flawed? Why hasn’t there been a systematic and scalable way to create software that is easy to use, robust, and secure?

Examining these issues in depth, The Essence of Software introduces a theory of software design that gives new answers to old questions. Daniel Jackson shows how a software system can be viewed as a collection of interacting concepts. Through this radical and original perspective, Jackson lays out a practical path, accessible to anyone—from strategist and marketer to UX designer, architect, or programmer—for making software that is empowering, dependable, and a delight to use.

Princeton University Press / November 2021

title: Open 10-player CS:GO dataset for multiplayer world models
description: Thousands of hours of frame-aligned, 10-player first-person gameplay with full game state — free for research, so anyone can train multiplayer world models.
fullText:
World models keep popping up. Nobody has cracked multiplayer at scale, because multiplayer data is painful to gather. It takes three things, all on the same clock:

We put in the work. Vortech is a tiny team of 3 people, racks of GPU instances, and a couple years of plumbing. Below is what came out of it.

Thousands of hours of 10-player first-person gameplay, free, so anyone can start building multiplayer world models. Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, for non-commercial research and education.

One bot round from the dataset, recorded from all ten players at once. Every view, every number and every hit sits on the same 16 Hz clock — pick a player and watch the others see them.

The data comes from a pipeline that turns Source-engine games into unlimited multiplayer data, for anyone who holds the licence to the game, or is Valve itself. These games ship with bots and GOTV, a built-in recorder that captures every tick of every match. That is a perfect setup for automated data production: no players to recruit, no screens to capture.

First run: CS:GO, one map, 33 servers, five days. Gameplay generation scales linearly with compute. Other Source titles plug into the same steps, given the rights to them.

We have been training a multiplayer world model on this for a while.It draws the next frame for each of the ten players, while a server keeps them all in the same game.It is a work in progress; we will put it out when it is good enough.

Meanwhile, a sneak peek: the recorded game on the left, the model on the right.

Parquet + MP4, no pre-made splits, CC BY-NC 4.0 for non-commercial research. It lands on Hugging Face; this link becomes the dataset itself the day it goes up.

dataset spec get it on hugging face

Control and scale. We pick the map, the rules and the player count, and servers run around the clock. Expert bots move and fight plausibly enough to teach a model the physics, the map and the combat.

Source games record complete demos by design, replay them deterministically, and can re-render any player's view after the fact. That is what makes ten aligned POVs per match possible. And if it has to be a Source game, it might as well be CS.

Per 16 Hz step: actions, poses, health, weapons and damage events for all ten players, plus 256×256 first-person video for the rendered subset. All of it is one map, aim_map_usp_s by im0rtus, with USPs on the CT side and Glocks on the T side. That is far from enough to build a world model of Counter-Strike; it is enough to experiment with, and to focus on the multiplayer part of world models. See the dataset spec.

No. Everything here, the game-state tables, the videos and the code, is CC BY-NC 4.0: free for non-commercial research and education, as long as you credit Vortech. The videos also show Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, which belongs to Valve, and we cannot grant any rights to Valve’s game. If you have a commercial use in mind, write to us; for the footage you would need Valve’s licence too.

It'll be done when it's done. No date.

Questions about the data, ideas for it, or something you are building on it: write to us. hello@vor.tech

title: Flock Cameras Lead Police to Identify Wrong Car in Road Rage Case
description: A driver told Lexington, Kentucky police that a dark-colored Ram 2500 had been involved in a road-rage incident, so police turned to Flock to find it.
fullText:
Imagine police surrounding your house and knocking on your door early in the morning, suspecting you of a crime you didn't commit. That's what happened to Will Penn, Robin Pen, and Penn's 94-year-old grandmother, reports Lexington, Kentucky's Lex News. As is so often the case these days, this was a case of mistaken identity, spurred by a Flock camera.

The couple's Ring camera captured the sequence of events. At 3:56 a.m., several Lexington police cars began to surround their property. At 4:08, they shone their spotlights on the house, and armed police knocked on the door. Penn and Pen went outside to speak with them, which was when they learned what this was all about.

"There was an incident tonight in which the vehicle we are trying to find is nearly identical to yours," an officer said — a road rage incident the victim had reported, describing a dark Ram 2500 without giving a license plate number. The Flock system told police it could be Penn's truck. Per Lex News:

The victim gave a detailed accounting of the events which included a description of the suspect and the suspect's vehicle," [Lexington Police Commander Daniel] Burnett said.

Officers showed the Flock image of the vehicle to the victim, who confirmed it.

"The officers actually showed an image of that vehicle to the victim. The victim was very confident that that was the same vehicle," Burnett said.

The couple told police they had just returned from a taco truck. It may have been 4 a.m., but it's always a good time for a taco, so this seems completely plausible. Police believed them and said they were not in trouble. That didn't exactly calm the damage to their nerves, though. "My blood pressure didn't go down for about an hour until after the incident," Pen said. And Penn added: "My grandmother was scared to death."

Unlike many other cases where Flock's system actively identifies the wrong vehicle, this seems like police put too much faith in the information Flock gave them. By their own admission, the vehicle description was vague: no license plate number, and a dark-colored Ram 2500. The victim didn't even give an exact color. I'm not blaming them; it was dark, and they may not have been able to tell exactly which dark color it was, especially while they felt they were in danger.

It's up to police to take that into account, though, and not simply jump on the first easy lead they get. Along with a picture of Penn's truck they had the location and the time it passed by the Flock camera. Could the road rager have plausibly gotten there from the victim's reported time and location? We don't know. It seems like police found the first hit that potentially matched, then showed it to the victim. The confirmation bias is strong with this one. Plus, we all know the Ram 2500 is an exceptionally rare vehicle, especially dark ones. They might as well have been looking for a red Miata at an autocross.

Yet Lexington police stand by their methodology and tactics. The multiple police cars were appropriate for responding to a felony assault, Burnett said, and officers were simply checking out a lead provided by Flock cameras, "like lots of other information that law enforcement has access to."

Burnett is correct about that last part. Flock's vast network of spy cameras taking an unimaginably huge number of pictures is a powerful tool, but an imperfect one. Combine that with an understandably imperfect vehicle description, and police had little chance of finding the right truck, even with Flock's capabilities. Instead of accepting that, they went with the first truck they found, disturbing a couple and a 94-year-old grandmother in the middle of the night.

"I feel like they're not doing their investigation work properly like they used to and they're just jumping the gun on it," Penn told Lex News. It could be worse, though. At least the truck was a similar color to the one reported. At least police believed Penn and Pen and they didn't spend 86 hours in solitary because police believed Flock over them. It's only a matter of time until someone gets killed this way.

title: Memory safety for Postgres extensions in C/C++
description: How ClickHouse’s Postgres extensions handle the memory safety challenges of combining C and C++, from clean language boundaries to isolated helper processes.
fullText:
We’ve developed a few postgres extensions at ClickHouse:

All of these involved bringing C++ into a Postgres extension. Postgres is C. Surely C & C++ play nice together, right?

No. Postgres has its own memory allocation pattern built around MemoryContext. Instead of using malloc/free, one should use palloc/pfree. These functions associate allocations with a MemoryContext, which can work as an arena allocator freeing everything at the end of a transaction or aggregate or what have you. MemoryContexts can also have callbacks to act as destructors. Postgres handles failed memory allocations by raising an error, for which it has a whole PG_TRY/PG_CATCH/PG_FINALLY macro package built on setjmp/longjmp. PG_FINALLY is another method of building RAII-like destructor logic.

C++ code on the other hand tends to use new/delete, which invokes constructors/destructors, & raises std::bad_alloc on failed allocation. These two systems do not interact well: setjmp/longjmp skips C++ cleanup; jumping past nontrivial destructors for automatic objects is undefined behavior, not merely a leak. PG_FINALLY and MemoryContext callbacks do not make such a jump safe. Exceptions bypass PG_CATCH/PG_FINALLY. Worse, an uncaught exception causes the process to abort, which even in a background worker will lead to the Postgres postmaster process having to restart everything in fear that shared memory has been corrupted.

Each of these extensions took a different strategy around memory safety.

For pg_clickhouse we have completely eradicated the use of C++. This involved replacing clickhouse-cpp with an entirely new C library, clickhouse-c, which we recently wrapped in another library, pg-clickhouse-c, in order to consolidate postgres logic while keeping clickhouse-c a general-purpose library. clickhouse-c was designed to be transport-agnostic, supporting Native format outside Native protocol, so now the HTTP driver shares much of its decoding/encoding logic with the binary driver by using Native format over HTTP. For HTTP we use libcurl, which offers a low level enough interface to play nice with Postgres's environment.

For example, previously in binary.cpp, make_datum converted a ClickHouse String with:

cstring_to_text_with_len allocates a Postgres text value with palloc. If that allocation fails, Postgres raises ERROR and jumps to its error handler, bypassing s's destructor. Surrounding C++ try/catch cannot catch this jump.

For pg_re2 C++ is scoped to re2_wrapper.cpp. All C++ allocations happen within C++ try/catch, & it doesn't call into postgres C code. Separation of concerns is sufficient for this encapsulation to draw a clean line between the two systems.

pg_chdb reuses pg-clickhouse-c for decoding/encoding native blocks. Originally it loaded libchdb into the background worker, but eventually moved libchdb into a separate helper executable. Isolating libchdb is the point: its C++ runtime, threads, allocations, and failures live outside a Postgres backend or managed background worker. The backend forks and execs this helper, so it remains a descendant of postmaster, but postmaster does not manage it as a background worker. This helper only needs enough information to run a ClickHouse query & exchange Native blocks, so it has no need for postgres headers. A libchdb crash can then fail the calling operation without itself triggering Postgres cluster crash recovery.

pg_stat_ch relies on OpenTelemetry libraries & Arrow's C++ bindings, as nanoarrow lacks many IPC features. C++ code is isolated to a Postgres background worker which we then instrument with C++ exception handling & PG exception handling. A terminate handler routes uncaught exceptions / std::terminate through ereport(FATAL) instead of default abort() / SIGABRT. FATAL normally runs Postgres process-exit cleanup and exits with status 1. Postmaster accepts this as a non-crash exit if shared-memory detachment also completes cleanly; worker restart then follows bgw_restart_time. By contrast, abnormal worker termination can trigger cluster-wide crash recovery and disconnect other sessions.

This is a mitigation, not a general crash-isolation guarantee. FATAL cannot repair inconsistent shared memory, and failed cleanup can still make postmaster treat exit as a crash. A process-wide terminate handler also needs scrutiny if invoked by a library thread: it does not make Postgres error handling and exit callbacks safe to call from arbitrary threads.

Writing this blog exposed a concrete ownership problem, addressed in PR #126: an interrupted dequeue could leave a slot pointing to already-freed error text or already-released query text. Recovery retries the slot before tail advances, potentially freeing or releasing the same reference twice. Long term moving C++ dependencies into a helper executable, as done in pg_chdb, will further harden pg_stat_ch. PR #129 is the first step: isolate C++ in src/exporter with no Postgres dependency and let bgworker.c handle the C/C++ boundary.

title: Sean Parker is rebuilding Stability AI around music
description: Sean Parker, who once taught the music industry what asking for forgiveness looks like, is now back with the labels' blessing and money.
fullText:
Sean Parker, the Napster co-founder, has jumped back into the music industry, and he tells The Information that he’s playing by the rules this time. (Asking for forgiveness rather than permission didn’t work out so well last time around, he readily concedes.)

Two years ago, he joined an $80 million rescue of Stability AI, the image-generator startup that nearly collapsed after overspending and internal turmoil led to founder Emad Mostaque’s ouster. Now Parker and his longtime friend Prem Akkaraju, who became CEO, are taking the wraps off what they’ve been building.

The big idea, Parker says, is to turn Stability into the go-to AI toolmaker for music professionals. Toward that end, in late August, the company announced $76 million in funding from, among others, Sony, Warner, and Universal, which also licensed their catalogs for training as part of the deal. Stability has since released three new audio models and AI music-editing software. The AI can generate whole instrumental tracks or short snippets from text prompts. Parker says an upcoming update will let users hum a melody or beatbox a drum pattern to steer it.

title: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes doc is a modern masterpiece of deceit
description: No spoilers here – TV’s grand illusionist meets his match when he moves in with Theranos founder and her family
fullText:
New York film festival: No spoilers here – TV’s grand illusionist meets his match when he moves in with Theranos founder and her family

For anyone remotely near the worlds of documentary, comedy or medical fraud, there has been one thing on the mind for weeks now: a single-minute clip of Nathan Fielder, the absurdist comedian whose boundary-pushing HBO series The Rehearsal cemented his status as docu-reality’s premier auteur, staring into the deep blue eyes of Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of the blood-testing startup Theranos. Unblinking, faces inches apart, the famously dry purveyor of harebrained business schemes and the convicted fraudster appeared locked in a battle of wills. “Are you being real right now?” Fielder asked her, in a classically meta bit – could Fielder really have spent years filming a secret documentary with one of Silicon Valley’s most notorious pariahs?

The prospect of TV’s grand illusionist versus emblematic girl-boss scammer seemed potentially too good to be true; buzz for You Can See Everything, Fielder’s furtive documentary co-directed with wunderkind du jour Lance Oppenheim (whose narrative feature debut, the Robert Pattinson-starring Primetime, premiered last month) was such that access to the film’s New York film festival premiere on Wednesday became this fall’s hottest ticket.

Those who were there can confirm: the hype is deserved. You Can See Everything is, somehow, more shocking, twistier, thornier and revealing than billed – a stupefying and gloriously destabilizing hall of psychological mirrors, a thrilling once-in-a-lifetime collision of director and subject. You know from the minute Billy Evans, Holmes’s shifty husband-cum-business partner who entered the picture post-Theranos, claims that “the best way for people to see who she is … is to give as much access as possible into our daily lives”, while lying with Holmes on a playroom floor, that you’re in for a wild ride. My mouth was agape for, conservatively, one half of the film’s unusually deserved three-hour run time.

Let me say now, if you’ve made it this far: I will not spoil major shifts – and if you are at all familiar with the Fielder canon, you know they’re coming – for a singular movie whose enjoyment depends, in part, on an element of surprise, both for viewers and for film-makers who genuinely seem to not know what they signed up for when they walked into the Holmes-Evans household rental in 2023. Arguably the less you know about anything that is to come, the better.

What I can tell you is that You Can See Everything is a masterpiece of who’s playing who, the fragility and absurdities of trust, seemingly begotten by chance. Back in 2023, convicted of wire fraud and conspiracy and awaiting the start of her 11-year sentence in prison, Holmes, along with Evans – who appears to be her match made in heaven, as neither ever blink and are maybe always lying – sought out a film crew to document their life with their two young children, in an attempt to protest her innocence and, perhaps, rebrand for Theranos 2.0. For some reason, they chose Oppenheim, a documentarian whose distinctive style – hyper-saturation, tight frames, creeping zooms – exposes the eerie in the mundane, and Fielder, whose precise style of spectrum-y, extreme cringe means that no question will be off the table. As Fielder points out on camera, in one of several exquisitely blunt confrontations, it is an odd choice to allow a comedian famous for his business scams to make a documentary that will supposedly clear your name of arguably the most famous fraud scandal of the 2010s.

The result is a three-hour documentary filmed like a thriller and scored like a drama that plays like an unraveling of certainty in real time. Oppenheim’s house style, shots tightly hugging then boring into a face with laser-like curiosity, perfectly suits the material; scenes that could be an unlikely tableau instead become a fascinating parade of inscrutable motivations, isolated actors bristling against the others. There is something extremely satisfying in watching Fielder’s sharp angles – arched eyebrows, needling questions, dispensation of social buffers – tangle with Holmes’s disposition (or performance? or genuine personality?) of guileless warmth, a strange and compelling chemistry building within a reality distortion field. If Fielder’s earlier work felt at times like it was punching down, trading on the naivety of regular people, well, he has finally met his match.

I am, admittedly, writing around a film that must be seen to be discussed, and will surely engender much chatter as to what, exactly, we just witnessed. But trust that things devolve in a very Fielderian spiral, into a dissection of the form unlike anything I have ever seen or, as things get going and participants either lose their filters or sharpen their game, anything I have ever hoped to see when it comes to the figure known as Elizabeth Holmes. Trust, too, that if there was a question you were hoping to ask Holmes or, moreover, her husband – did he really have no reservations when he met the disgraced founder at a party in 2017, at the height of her scandal? – it gets asked, and then some (I did not need to know about conjugal visits, or lack thereof, in the Texas prison where Holmes continues to reside).

Trust, ultimately, that you can see more than you ever imagined you’d see about Elizabeth Holmes and maybe get no closer to discerning the truth – and yet it will all be worth it.

You Can See Everything screened at the New York film festival and will be released in the US on 16 October with UK and Australian release dates to be announced
