fullText:
TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

The suspect is Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East told NBC News. Authorities have not officially released the identity.

The Wall Street Journal, citing sources familiar with the matter, reported that al-Hammami had “previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views.”

Oman Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether he previously worked for the company.

Emirati officials are leading investigations into the midair incident, which occurred Wednesday on a flight carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials, when crew and passengers were able to enter the cabin and subdue the attacker.

“Investigations into the incident aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act,” UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in an update on Saturday.

“The co-pilot began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls,” he said.

Al-Hammami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi on Thursday, the Saudi Interior Ministry said. The statement said his health had “improved,” but his medical condition was unclear.

Al Shamsi said investigations were ongoing to “establish the full circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident.”

Israeli government spokesman David Mencer said Friday that Israeli investigators would “join their Emirati counterparts in investigating this attempted mass murder and establishing precisely what happened, his motives and background.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday: “As time passes, the picture becomes clearer: The attacker had undergone Islamist radicalization. He came to crash the plane, along with its passengers.”

He did not say how he reached that conclusion, but added: “We are investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.”

Netanyahu’s spokesman Doron Spielman told NBC News that the suspect “talks on his social media about killing Jews.”

The flight captain, Indian national Capt. Smit Machchhar, spoke for the first time Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi.

Machchhar was widely praised for his efforts to prevent the plane from crashing by opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crew members to rush in.

Speaking from his hospital bed, Machchhar said he had been “severely injured” and “could sense that the aircraft was going down.”

“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, adding that he told himself to “give just one last push” to the cockpit door.

The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi called Machchhar the “Indian braveheart,” saying in an X post Saturday that he “remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well.”

The deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, Hamdan bin Mohammed, posted photos on X after visiting Machchhar in the hospital in which he’s seen kissing the pilot’s head and shaking his hand. Machchhar, with one arm in a cast and medical dressings on his head, appears awake and smiling.

“From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise,” he wrote.

Ayelet Epstein, a 47-year-old Israeli, told NBC News that her 14-year-old daughter asked if they were going to die when they heard shouting and “a huge fall started.”

“I told her, no, I don’t think so, we’re going to be OK,” she said, adding that “I was trying to rationalize things in a hopeful way for her.”

Epstein thanked Machchhar “from the bottom of my heart” for saving their lives, lauding his bravery.

A Flydubai spokesperson said Saturday: “We recognise that there are many questions at this stage; however, the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation. We are therefore not in a position to comment further beyond our published statements.”

“We remain fully committed to supporting the ongoing investigation and are in close coordination with the relevant government authorities and regulators,” the spokesperson added.

President Donald Trump told reporters Thursday that there would be renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack.

“You just ask them,” he said. “They know what happened. They’ll be hit very hard.”

There are no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack, a senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation told NBC News.

Raf Sanchez and Shira Pinson reported from Tel Aviv. Freddie Clayton reported from London. Tom Winter and Jonathan Dienst reported from New York.

title: Ohio factory layoffs test Trump's economic pitch in a working-class stronghold
description:
— Sipping tea from beer mugs with his coworkers, Kyle Bos listed the ways his life is changing.
Bos has two daughters, with a third due in January. At the grocery store, five items cost as much as a full cart once did. And on Wednesday, Bos and nearly 1,400 other people were laid off from their jobs at what had been the Navistar truck factory in southwestern Ohio.
The layoffs — occurring just three days before Donald Trump’s rally on Saturday at a nearby high school — were large enough to basically erase an entire year of job growth in the greater Dayton, Ohio area.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Sipping tea from beer mugs with his coworkers, Kyle Bos listed the ways his life is changing.

Bos has two daughters, with a third due in January. At the grocery store, five items cost as much as a full cart once did. And on Wednesday, Bos and nearly 1,400 other people were laid off from their jobs at what had been the Navistar truck factory in southwestern Ohio.

The layoffs — occurring just three days before Donald Trump's rally on Saturday at a nearby high school — were large enough to basically erase an entire year of job growth in the greater Dayton, Ohio area. And they are one reason why Bos, 30, plans to spend the final weeks before the November election canvassing votes for Democrats.

Asked how many times he voted for Trump, Bos held up three tattooed fingers. But he said he's done with the president.

"Something has to change politically in this country," said Bos, a member of the United Auto Workers who identifies as a centrist.

This year's election is a test for the working-class coalition that lifted Trump into the White House and gave majorities to Republicans in the House and Senate. The outcome will be decided in places like Dayton, which once sprouted factories but shed about half of its 90,000 factory jobs since 1990 after the North American Free Trade Agreement and trade with China made it cheaper to buy auto parts from abroad.

Trump's blunt talk and status as a celebrity businessman initially helped him around Dayton, where voters sensed that politics as usual had failed them. But voters this year are disgruntled about inflation and the war in Iran.

An Ohio race could help determine control of the Senate. Republican Sen. Jon Husted is facing a challenge from former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, who is trying to harness that disenchantment as he attempts a comeback two years after losing his seat.

Trump's visit to the Dayton area is one of what he says will be a 32-day marathon of rallies to try to convince the public that the economy is better than they think.

"All over the country, they're building factories, plants, manufacturing's coming back," Trump said on Thursday. "The only thing we're doing badly at is public relations."

Americans increasingly blame Trump for the high cost of living, though Trump has largely sneered at concerns about affordability. However, he has promised to give people $5,000 checks if Republicans win the House and Senate next month— something Bos said he found offensive.

"It feels like a bribe, a slap in the face, and, like, that we're all ignorant," Bos said.

In the 1990s, as steady paychecks vanished, drug addiction and crime increased. Things seemed to hit bottom after the 2008 financial crisis, prompting Phil Plummer — who was then Montgomery County Sheriff — to enter politics.

"My jail was 40% drug addicts, 50% mental health patients, 10% criminals," said Plummer, the Montgomery County GOP chairman who has been a Republican state representative since 2019. "We got it upside down — that's what drove me to the state house."

Plummer, the Montgomery County Republican chairman, is now on the ballot for the Ohio state Senate and said he thinks Trump is what keeps the GOP's coalition of businesses and working-class families together.

In recent years, the local economy has improved as the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base steadily added government workers. The base has drawn new aerospace companies to the area such as Joby Aviation, Electra and the Sierra Nevada Corporation.

"In economic development, it takes time, and you have got to give it a little bit of time to bake, and then once it does, then you're going to have something special," said Jeff Hoagland, CEO of the Dayton Development Coalition.

The White House pointed to the $850 million investment by aircraft maker Electra — along with announcements in Ohio from Honda, Stellantis and others — as evidence Trump's policies were creating jobs.

But at the former Navistar plant, Trump's broad tariffs never boosted demand and the plant's former owner, International Motors, chose to offload the facility.

Trump's major legislative achievement — the One Big, Beautiful Bill — contributed little to people's take-home pay, even as it temporarily stripped taxes from tips and overtime.

"We weren't getting a lot of overtime because of the economy," said Marianne Donnelly, who drove a forklift at the factory. "There just wasn't any to be had, very little to be had."

Laid-off workers like Donnelly say they expect to be rehired in six to 12 months by Roshel, a Canadian manufacturer of armored vehicles, which is buying the plant. Roshel said in a statement that it's "working with everyone involved not only to protect the current workforce, but to more than double it over the coming years through a phased process."

On the Monday before the layoffs, Morgan Hughes and JoJo Burkhard were knocking on doors in Kettering, a Dayton suburb. They were trying to convince union members and retirees to vote for Democrats.

The Navistar job had helped Hughes, 35, buy a house at age 21 and work alongside her father. Burkhard said inflation had made it easier to swing voters to their side.

"It isn't a hard pitch at all," she said. "And even if they don't want to stay Democratic long term, they'll at least give the candidates a chance this election, which could be a turning point for us."

After a morning of talking to voters, the pair settled down at a Chinese restaurant for some potstickers and the weight of the week hit them.

Burkhard cracked open a fortune cookie and tears began to well up. The layoffs meant no work for her, her boyfriend and her mother — and the words in small print almost seemed prophetic.

Her fortune read: "You'll find your inner strength to overcome challenges."

title: 'Different' Morrison gives NI new option
description: Northern Ireland's Kieran Morrison hopes he has earned the trust of manager Michael O'Neill after impressing on his first international start.
fullText:
Northern Ireland's Kieran Morrison hopes he has earned the trust of manager Michael O'Neill after impressing on his first international start.

The Liverpool winger, who is spending this season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, provided the assist for Isaac Price for the side's second goal in an eye-catching 3-0 Nations League win over Ukraine in Slovakia.

The 19-year-old was one of three changes made by O'Neill for the game in Trnava and impressed in an inside forward role off the right-hand side.

An unused substitute for the first two games of Group B2 in which Northern Ireland took four points against Georgia and Hungary, Morrison was pleased to quickly repay O'Neill's faith.

"I've been biding my time after the first two games," he told BBC Sport NI's Gavin Andrews.

"I was training well, working hard and I'm glad he [O'Neill] trusts me enough to give me the start. I think I did well enough."

Who has 'no ceiling' as Northern Ireland shine in Nations League?

Brown scores two as superb Northern Ireland stun Ukraine

While Price, who nodded home Morrison's cross for his 11th international goal, is nailed on for one of the roles behind the central striker in O'Neill's preferred system, Morrison certainly staked a claim to hold on to the other against Georgia at Windsor Park on Monday night.

"Thought he was really good," said Price of Morrison.

"He's a different threat than what we have had before. A really good crosser of the ball and he has come in and given the manager a headache with a game on Monday."

Despite the praise for his delivery, Morrison added that putting the ball into the box was not his first instinct.

"To be fair I wasn't going to cross it," he said.

"I was like 'OK, get the ball and do some stepovers', but it was just set it back to me and I whipped it in and Isaac was there.

"Every time I got the ball, I was just trying to make something happen."

Morrison, who represented England at underage level but qualifies for Northern Ireland through his Newry-born mother, is hoping to keep his place for Monday and make what would be a first home outing for the side.

"It's going to be great," said the player who made two senior Liverpool appearances last season.

"I've never played at Windsor Park. Hopefully I get the start, if I don't get the start, hopefully I come on and impact it."

title: Baxter backs Slade after missed kicks at Bath
description: Exeter boss Rob Baxter urges Henry Slade not to dwell on his missed kicks in their loss at Bath.
fullText:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter has urged Henry Slade not to dwell on his missed kicks in their loss at Bath.

Slade missed two first-half conversions before hitting the post with a penalty late in the second half as Chiefs went down 40-34 in a thrilling game at the Rec.

Team-mate Harvey Skinner stepped up to kick a 79th-minute penalty for Exeter that secured a losing bonus point as Baxter's side search for a first win of the season.

"I think we've been very fortunate with Henry over the years, but particularly last year," Baxter told BBC Radio Devon as Slade practised kicks after the final whistle.

"You think how many clutch kicks in big games he's knocked over for us and kept us in games, pushed us through things and just taking those real pressure kicks and he's always stood up and done it. You know there's going to be the odd game.

"But the most important thing for him is he shakes it off.

"I'd rather he wasn't out here practising now and he just goes and sits and has a beer and chills out because I don't think this is the way for him to get out of his system.

"But I'll have a chat with him as I walk past now and tell him to get in there and enjoy being with the lads, because he's too good a player for this to be an issue."

Bath gain revenge on Exeter to win 11-try thriller

Exeter reached last season's Prem final, where they lost to Northampton at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

But they have yet to record a win this season after a surprising loss at home to Gloucester last week.

Baxter says his side's loss at Bath, and their sticky start to the season, should not cause too much concern yet.

"In a way, I'll be worried that we think we have to get five points second game of the season to be competitive," he said.

"What I want us to do is go, 'We play really well every week, we build our points score', that's what gets us where we need to be.

"We saw that last year - that's what we've got to do again."

title: Republic of Ireland news conference ends abruptly amid accusations
description: Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match news conference ends abruptly as accusations are levelled at his players.
fullText:
For more than 11 minutes of Saturday's pre-match news conference, Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson fielded questions centred on Sunday's Nations League Group B3 'home' game against Israel in Serbia.

The Icelander revealed that Dara O'Shea - captain in place of the injured Nathan Collins - was not with the squad, as his wife was due to give birth. He may arrive back in Backa Topola prior to Sunday's 19:45 BST kick-off.

Hallgrimsson also gave his thoughts on the strain of this four-game international window and reflected on Thursday's 2-2 draw against Austria.

As the first section of the media conference, which is allowed to be broadcast live, was ending, the mood soured.

One reporter tried to quiz Hallgrimsson on his thoughts about the incident on Wednesday when a co-pilot attacked a pilot on a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.

The Republic of Ireland manager was also asked by another journalist about alleged racism by Irish players during last Sunday's 3-0 win over Israel in Hungary and refused to give up the microphone.

Promptly, the news conference was brought to a close by Football Association of Ireland (FAI) head of communications Kieran Crowley after calling those allegations "completely untrue".

The allegations of racism by an Irish player comes after it was confirmed the FAI is investigating reports of racist abuse directed towards Republic of Ireland striker Adam Idah by Israel fans in Debrecen.

Minutes before the news conference was brought to an abrupt halt, Hallgrimsson insisted he would not be drawn on either matter and would not "get involved in that as others will process that".

"It is a game with a lot of emotions attached," Hallgrimsson said.

"I haven't read anything and it's not something I want to get involved with. It goes to a process, both in our department and with Uefa.

"Something was reported by both teams so I just hope we can focus on football and football will be the winner after this.

"I have not gone into details looking at this as I have enough to think about."

Second Israel game won't be a friendly - Hallgrimsson

Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious

The Republic of Ireland boss revealed the team have taken to a group prayer before leaving the dressing room before recent games "just to cool our heads before we go on to the pitch" and said that has been led by midfielder Conor Coventry whom he joked is now known within the squad as "Brother Coventry".

It has been a challenging international window for the Republic of Ireland with the Israel double-header dominating discourse in Irish football.

Since the teams were drawn together in February, a 'Stop The Game' campaign was launched by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine to boycott the fixtures in protest of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war.

Before last week's 'home' game for Israel in Hungary, goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the fixtures, saying "it would be wrong to participate" while a vote by players to play the games passed by a "significant majority", according to FAI chief executive David Courell.

There were protests during the game against Austria in Dublin on Thursday, with tennis balls thrown on to the pitch and a protester briefly interrupting the game when he ran on to the turf, waving a Palestine flag.

Hallgrimmson said under the circumstances, it will be a "a big win for this group and the association if we go through undamaged".

"The most pleasing thing for me is to see the togetherness and how they stand up for each other. Whatever they have done, they have done it with respect to the situation, to each other and after this, this bond of brothers will be stronger than ever. All the obstacles this group will face in the future will be lesser than it is.

"When we look back, this camp will be a moment we grew the most and stepped up as leaders, supported each other and stuck together. The power of togetherness is stronger than individuals."

title: Ospreys hit by Lions' second-half show of power
description: Ospreys beaten in Johannesburg after six-try Lions turn around half-time deficit in the United Rugby Championship.
fullText:
Tries: Cronje, Botha, Brandon, Chamberlain, Mpeku 2 Con: Smith Pens: Smith

Tries: K Williams, Daniel, Moriarty Cons: Edwards 2

Ospreys were comprehensively beaten by six-try Lions after a second-half onslaught at Ellis Park in the United Rugby Championship.

Mark Jones' Ospreys started the 2026-27 season by claiming a four-try bonus point in defeat by Sharks in Durban, but they left Johannesburg without anything to show for their efforts on Saturday.

Ospreys led 12-10 at half-time after responding excellently to Erich Cronje's opener with tries by Keiran Williams and Efan Daniel.

But Lions, who enjoyed set-piece dominance, had their four-try bonus secured before the hour thanks to PJ Botha, Morne Brandon and Boeta Chamberlain.

Kelly Mpeku added two more for Lions, while Ospreys scored their third through Ross Moriarty with the final play.

An off-day from the kicking tee for the prolific Lions fly-half Chris Smith, who could only manage one conversion and a penalty, prevented this from being an absolute hammering.

Ospreys have the consolation of knowing their South Africa tour is out of the way early on.

They now return to Wales for a derby against Dragons at Rodney Parade on Friday, 9 October (19:45 BST).

Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

Ospreys won against Lions at altitude in Johannesburg in the 2023-24 Challenge Cup, but repeating that in the URC was always going to be a long shot.

The hosts lost just once on home soil last season – to South African rivals Bulls – and started the current campaign with victory against Leinster.

The only score of a scrappy first quarter was a penalty by Smith, with Ospreys turning down opportunities to level in favour of hunting a try.

It was Lions who were first to cross in the 28th minute through wing Cronje after an incisive attack from turnover ball.

Ospreys responded well and struck back, also from turnover ball, when centre Williams cut a nice line to finish powerfully from midfield partner Evardi Boshoff's offload.

It got better when they exploited Lions' indiscipline to get a second try with the last play of the half through hooker Daniel from a driving line-out.

Opposite number Botha and replacement Brandon scored through the same method soon after the restart to get the home side back on track.

Lions got their bonus point in the 57th minute when full-back Chamberlain crossed, with Francke Horn's athletic offload deemed to have been flat.

Wales fly-half Dan Edwards was yellow-carded for a high tackle on the hour, and the hosts turned the screw with wing Mpeku going over twice down the right.

Replacement flanker Moriarty did prevent Ospreys from suffering a scoreless second half, but this was another statement of intent by Lions at home in their bid to qualify for successive play-offs.

title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia
description: Even Lewis Hamilton fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
fullText:
Even Lewis Hamilton, starting from his equal best grid position of the year in second place, fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Verstappen has dominated the weekend so far on Formula 1's return to the Sepang track for the first time since 2017.

Hamilton joins him on the front row to revive memories of their no-holds-barred title battle five years ago.

But at nearly 0.3 seconds slower in qualifying, and with the pace Verstappen has shown all weekend, Hamilton's mindset on Saturday was to "just try my best to hold on to him tomorrow".

This was Verstappen's first pole position of the year - a remarkable statistic for someone who came within two points of winning a fifth world title last year after one of the all-time great fightbacks.

Red Bull started the year off the pace - the car was on average more than 0.5secs a lap slower than Mercedes in the first half of the year - and for a time there were questions as to whether Verstappen would stick around for 2027.

But after being courted by McLaren, Verstappen signed a two-year contract extension over the summer break, saying he believed in the Red Bull project and didn't mind putting in the work to turn things around.

Verstappen arrived in Malaysia after a run of three consecutive podium finishes, and with Red Bull hoping to prove out an upgrade that had seen them finish less than 0.2secs off victory in Baku last Sunday.

In the tropical heat of Malaysia, around the demanding long corners of this track with perhaps the roughest surface of the season, the upgrade - centred on a new floor - has more than proved its worth.

"It's been an incredible result for us," Verstappen said. "Looking at the season, how it started for us and the progression that we have made. At some tracks we were kind of close, but now I think this weekend it was very positive for us.

"We have been adding bits to the car and they have worked. It's simple as that. When they work, you gain lap time, you have a better overall balance in the car.

"So with tyres that are very sensitive to balance, that gives you also more lap time.

"And then on a track probably where it's all very hot and you want a, let's say, stable balance or connected balance, then that's very important. And that's what we have found a little bit more over the last weekends."

Team-mate Isack Hadjar, who missed the first three races after the summer break with a wrist broken while boxing as part of his training programme, says the car felt transformed when he returned in Baku last weekend.

"I jumped in a car that's way better than when I left it in Budapest," said the Frenchman, who qualified third, but will start eighth after a grid penalty for exceeding his permitted number of engine parts.

"Definitely, when you step out actually for three races and you come back, you actually notice a bigger difference. And the last two weekends have been surprising."

A good car balance should put Verstappen in a good place for a race that will be dominated by tyre degradation in the stifling heat, whether the threatened rain holds off or not.

Hamilton, for one, but also Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who under-performed slightly in qualifying because of a combination between an unusual tyre strategy and an error on an early run.

The world championship leader's fourth place becomes third on the grid with Hadjar's penalty, and he can usually be relied upon to be a factor in the race.

Antonelli's main focus will be his advantage over team-mate George Russell, who trails the Italian by 66 points and starts four places behind, his momentum from his Baku win stalled, and somewhat perplexed as to his and his team's lack of pace.

At Mercedes, the bigger question is over the aerodynamic upgrade they brought to the car this weekend.

Mercedes are lagging behind their rivals when it comes to developing their car this season, apparently at least in part because they front-loaded their spend early in the season.

But this first big update since the Canadian Grand Prix in June has not yet proved the step they had expected.

The question is whether that is to do with the parts themselves or the very specific conditions of this weekend, in the heat and on the rough track surface, which is putting the tyres through the mill, and massively limiting the useful laps teams can do in terms of set-up work.

Antonelli said: "With this new package, obviously the window of the way the car operates is different. So, we're trying to understand in which window the car performance is best, in the high-speed corner and low-speed corners.

"Our high-speed performance has been very strong this weekend. We were very quick in the high-speed, but in the low-speed we lacked. So, we need to understand why and try to move on and improve."

As for the race, Antonelli said: "Track position is going to be very important. Strategy is going to be really important.

"It's a race where we will attack. Because undercut (stopping first and gaining time on a rival on fresh tyres) is incredibly powerful.

"So whenever there's an opportunity, we should go for maybe an undercut and try to maximise our opportunity.

"Tomorrow might be two stops, three stops. We don't know. But the only thing we know is that it's going to be roasting hot out there."

title: Dodgers continue quest for World Series three-peat
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers will begin their MLB play-off campaign on Saturday, with the defending champions playing in a double-header live on the BBC.
fullText:
Los Angeles has been the centre of the baseball world over the past few years.

The LA Dodgers have built a star-studded roster in Major League Baseball, winning back-to-back championships in 2024 and 2025.

Celebrities and royalty have flocked to Dodger Stadium, which will also host the Olympic tournament as baseball returns to the Games for Los Angeles 2028.

And you can get a glimpse of the Hollywood vibe as the Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat in the MLB play-offs this weekend.

After earning a bye for the first round last week, it is time for the Dodgers to join the post-season party and they will be part of an MLB double-header live on the BBC.

Saturday's coverage begins with the Chicago White Sox visiting the Cleveland Guardians for the start of their American League Division Series (18:00 BST).

You can then experience all the sights and sounds from Dodger Stadium, one of MLB's most iconic venues, as the defending champions begin their National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves (21:00 BST).

Opened in 1962, Dodger Stadium is the biggest MLB arena with a capacity of 56,000, and this year 'Dodger baseball' has been one of the hottest tickets in town.

For the past two years the team's total home attendance has passed four million. This year they set a franchise record of 4,034,219 - an average of 49,805 fans per game.

The signings of two-way star Shohei Ohtani and pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto in 2024 helped boost the team's Asian fanbase, increasing Japanese tourism to LA and supplementing the loyal local support.

Actors Brad Pitt, Will Ferrell, Bryan Cranston, Jason Bateman and Rob Lowe are all regulars at Dodger Stadium, while Justin and Hailey Bieber have been spotted at multiple games.

NBA star LeBron James and NFL quarterback Justin Herbert both attended last year's World Series, along with Sydney Sweeney, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. Who will show up this weekend as LA hosts games one and two of the best-of-five series against Atlanta?

Having briefly been based in LA, Pierre Ducrey - sports director for the International Olympic Committee (IOC) - has also watched numerous games at Dodger Stadium and is "quite familiar with the atmosphere it can deliver".

"There's so many Dodger fans and they're very passionate about the team," he told BBC Sport. "They have an incredible venue and one thing I do know about baseball is this is the perfect home for a baseball tournament."

Ohtani rewrites history to send Dodgers to World Series

Why 'face of baseball' is on cusp of global stardom

The Dodgers aren't the only show in town. The LA Lakers are one of the biggest franchises in basketball's NBA, as are the LA Rams in American football's NFL.

The Rams won the Super Bowl in their own stadium in 2022 and are favourites to win the NFL's championship game when it returns to SoFi Stadium next February.

The stadium hosted eight World Cup games last summer and anticipation is growing that LA is set for a third straight World Series later this month.

"This is a city that lives and breathes sport and the Dodgers are a perfect example of that," said Ducrey. "The popularity of the franchise in LA cannot be underestimated."

Atlanta Braves @ Los Angeles Dodgers

Major League Baseball Division Series

Dodger Stadium, Los Angeles, CA

Live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app

The Dodgers secured the second seed in the National League after finishing the regular season with 100 wins and 62 losses.

The Milwaukee Brewers were the only MLB team with a better record (103-59) yet the Dodgers are favourites to win the World Series, ahead of the Brewers and New York Yankees.

The Dodgers have continued to make big-name signings, with pitcher Tarik Skubal the latest in a mid-season trade, and their recent success has got fans dreaming of the franchise's first-ever three-peat.

"The Dodgers are in a very good period," Ducrey added. "There is a big momentum for them, but the team would still be immensely followed whether they're successful or not.

"There's a very long history behind it, and a very big tradition for baseball in Los Angeles."

Chicago White Sox @ Cleveland Guardians

Major League Baseball Division Series

Progressive Field, Cleveland, OH

Live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app

Although Ohtani is a rare two-way player, the Dodgers' leading home-run hitter will not pitch again this year because of injuries.

Skubal is expected to start on Saturday and face Matt Olson, who led Atlanta with 41 home runs in the regular season and added another in Thursday's series-clinching win over the Philadelphia Phillies.

Either the Dodgers or the Braves will face Milwaukee or the San Diego Padres in the National League Championship Series (NLCS) - one step from the World Series.

Sixth seed Chicago have already upset the Houston Astros in the other half of the play-offs and either the White Sox or Cleveland will face the Tampa Bay Rays or Yankees in the American League Championship Series (ALCS).

The winners of the ALCS and NLCS will meet in the World Series, which is scheduled to begin on Friday, 23 October.

title: Croatia Ready to Bite Back vs England: Preview, TV Info & Prediction
description: Croatia host England in a pivotal UEFA Nations League Group A3 clash at Rujevica Stadion in Rijeka on Saturday. Kick-off is 6:00 p.m. local time (12:00 p.m.
fullText:
Croatia host England in a pivotal UEFA Nations League Group A3 clash at Rujevica Stadion in Rijeka on Saturday. Kick-off is 6:00 p.m. local time (12:00 p.m. ET). Both sides sit on three points after two matches, with England bouncing back from a loss to Spain by beating Czechia, and Croatia suffering a heavy 4-1 defeat to the world champions after an opening win over Czechia. It's the sixth meeting between these two countries in eight years, a stretch that includes Croatia's famous 2018 World Cup semifinal win, though England has taken the last three meetings since. In the high-stakes arena of international soccer, this feels like a classic "response" game for the hosts.

UEFA ordered this match played behind closed doors as punishment for crowd trouble involving Croatian supporters during their Nations League quarterfinal against France last year, a sanction handed down in May 2025 that also cost Croatia a travel ban for their away fans against Czechia last weekend. But "closed doors" comes with a loophole: UEFA rules allow children under 14 from schools and academies to attend free, under supervision, and Croatian football officials now expect between 5,500 and 6,000 kids to fill the 8,200-seat stadium, alongside roughly 100 England supporters let in through a special arrangement between UEFA and the FA. That puts the stadium somewhere around 70% full, just not with the kind of passionate, raucous Croatian crowd that would normally be considered a real advantage. Thomas Tuchel, whose last match in Croatia as Chelsea boss ended in a Champions League defeat in Zagreb, called it "never nice" to play behind closed doors and admitted it creates "a strange atmosphere," though he said he's glad the children get to attend. The two nations played a similarly empty, goalless draw at this same venue back in October 2018.

Croatia are missing defenders Josip Juranović and Martin Erlić through injury, with Erlić having aggravated a hamstring strain that already kept him out against Spain. Young centre-back Luka Vušković is expected to step in alongside Joško Gvardiol. Luka Modrić, still going strong at 41, is strongly tipped to return to the starting lineup after coming off the bench against Spain. Dion Beljo has been in sharp form and should lead the line, with Martin Baturina, who scored against England at this summer's World Cup, pushing hard for a start under Slaven Bilić. Croatia have conceded nine goals across their last five matches, a defensive issue Bilić still hasn't fully solved.

England will be without Nico O'Reilly, who has withdrawn through injury and won't feature again this window, so Lewis Hall continues at left-back. Jordan Pickford is set to return in goal after James Trafford started the first two games, with Tuchel confirming both keepers would get two starts each this window. Trent Alexander-Arnold is in line for a long-awaited return at right-back, Jude Bellingham is expected to start after coming off the bench midweek, and Ezri Konsa could return to central defence. Harry Kane, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka form a potent attacking threat for Tuchel's side.

Croatia have a long history of raising their level against strong opposition, and this is their third match of the international window, the point at which they often find their rhythm. England remain dangerous and well-organised under Tuchel, but the combination of Modrić's experience and Croatia's ability to frustrate bigger teams makes an upset realistic, even without a raucous home crowd behind them. Expect a tight, competitive contest. Prediction: Croatia 2-1 England.

Croatia: Livaković; Smolčić, Vušković, Gvardiol, Perišić; Modrić, Kovačić, P. Sučić; Baturina, Beljo, M. Pašalić

England: Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Konsa, Guéhi, Hall; Anderson, Garner; Saka, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

title: Cubs Handed Strong Seiya Suzuki Free Agency Prediction
description: The Chicago Cubs crashed out in the Wild Card Series against the San Diego Padres and now face major offseason decisions, including whether to re-sign Seiya Suzuki.Suzuki hit .270 with 147 hits, 26 home runs, 86 RBIs, and 96 runs scored this season for Chicago, per StatMuse. Meanwhile, in the two Wild Card games against […] The post Cubs Handed Strong Seiya Suzuki Free Agency Prediction appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Chicago Cubs crashed out in the Wild Card Series against the San Diego Padres and now face major offseason decisions, including whether to re-sign Seiya Suzuki.

Suzuki hit .270 with 147 hits, 26 home runs, 86 RBIs, and 96 runs scored this season for Chicago, per StatMuse. Meanwhile, in the two Wild Card games against the Padres, the veteran went 2-for-7 with one run and one walk.

Still, in a weak free-agent class, the 32-year-old could be in demand. As a result, Zachary Rotman of FanSided believes the Cubs will lose Suzuki in free agency this offseason.

"Seiya Suzuki signed a five-year deal with the Cubs ahead of the 2022 season, and it's safe to say he lived up to it," Rotman wrote in an Oct. 1 article. "He averaged 22 home runs, 73 RBI, and an .823 OPS over that span, proving to be a rock-solid middle-of-the-order hitter for Chicago. He's a player the Cubs should have an interest in re-signing, but will that actually happen?

"Not only is Suzuki already 32 years old, but he's one of the best position players in a remarkably weak free agency class. This will likely result in him receiving a contract that's longer and more expensive than the Cubs will or should want to give him. They probably won't keep both Suzuki and Ian Happ, and while Suzuki is the better player, Happ should come cheaper, which is music to Tom Ricketts' ears."

Meanwhile, FanSided's MLB insider Robert Murray has Suzuki as the second-best free agent behind Tarik Skubal. If the Cubs have to choose between Suzuki and Ian Happ, then Rotman will be right that the Japanese outfielder might be too expensive for Chicago to keep if there's a bidding war for him.

"Suzuki, 32, is one of the top bats on the market and has improved defensively in the corner outfield," Murray wrote in a Sept. 28 article. "He's hit at least 20 home runs in four consecutive seasons, with a career-high 32 in 2025, and will have plenty of interest from offense-needy teams — with an early report already linking the slugger to the Toronto Blue Jays."

Knowing this could be the end of the road for Suzuki with the Cubs, the outfielder reflected on his time in Chicago as he couldn't be part of a team that pushes for a deep playoff run, as they have fallen short when reaching the postseason.

"Just looking back on the five years, I don't know if I was able to reach the expectations that people had," Suzuki said through an interpreter in an Oct. 2 article (h/t Patrick Mooney of The Athletic). "Each year, there was frustration at the end of the year. Looking back at it, I felt like I did get better. I worked hard. The plus, this last year, was that my defense improved a lot with all that work I put in.

"Looking back, there's a lot of what-ifs: Did I meet the expectations that people had about me, that I had about myself?"

title: Arike Ogunbowale drops ‘rigged’ take on WNBA if Paige Bueckers is snubbed of major accolade
description: Paige Bueckers receives a massive nod from her Dallas Wings teammate, Arike Ogunbowale. The Dallas Wings are out of the 2026 playoffs following an underwhelming display in the first round against the Golden State Valkyries.
fullText:
Paige Bueckers receives a massive nod from her Dallas Wings teammate, Arike Ogunbowale.

The Dallas Wings are out of the 2026 playoffs following an underwhelming display in the first round against the Golden State Valkyries.

While Arike Ogunbowale did everything in her power to will the Wings through to the next round, the same cannot be said for Paige Bueckers, who struggled to shoot well in Game 3.

Despite Bueckers' abysmal 3-of-14 shooting and overall struggles in the postseason, Ogunbowale believes it would be a shame if her teammate doesn't get the nod for a major WNBA accolade.

Bueckers' Game 3 performance shouldn't cloud the voters' judgment about her terrific regular-season production; that's what Ogunbowale believes.

In fact, she went as far as saying that if Bueckers is snubbed from the 2026 All-WNBA First Team, the league is 'rigged.'

"Well, we got Paige. Generational player; she willed us throughout the whole season," Ogunbowale said. "Should be First Team WNBA. If not, I feel like that s___ rigged."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 5.9 assists per game, while shooting a solid 51.2% from the field and 41.0% from the three-point line.

Thanks to her production, the Wings finished the regular season as the seventh seed, with a 27-17 record. But was that enough to earn a nod to the All-WNBA First Team? Only time will tell.

title: Manchester United set to make debut in clash against Tottenham Hotspur
description: Carlos Baleba Debut Gives Manchester United Fresh Lift Ahead of TottenhamManchester United finally got Carlos Baleba on the pitch, and that matters. After a £70 million move from Brighton in the summ...
fullText:
Manchester United finally got Carlos Baleba on the pitch, and that matters. After a £70 million move from Brighton in the summer, the midfielder had yet to play a minute because of an ankle issue he carried into Old Trafford. On Friday, that wait ended in a behind-closed-doors 2-1 win over Lausanne Sport at Carrington.

For Michael Carrick, this was practical more than symbolic. United return to Premier League action next weekend against Tottenham, and Baleba now looks far closer to being a genuine option. He was on the bench for the 1-1 draw at Fulham, but remained unused as United drifted through a poor result in west London.

The Baleba debut gives United something they have lacked, energy and presence in midfield. At 22, he arrives with expectation because of the fee and because Carrick pushed to get him in as the final signing of his first permanent transfer window. The delay has been frustrating, but the important part now is availability.

There was more good news beyond Baleba. Matthijs de Ligt started in central defence, his first appearance since November last year after a serious back problem. He did not feature at all under Carrick after the head coach replaced Ruben Amorim in January last season, so this was overdue.

United's defence has looked vulnerable for too long, and De Ligt's return could help steady it. That does not solve everything, but it gives Carrick another senior option in an area where reliability has been scarce.

Harry Maguire and Matheus Cunha also featured, with several first-team players involved because they were not away on international duty. It was a low-key friendly, but the timing is useful. United do not need noise here, they need players back. Baleba and De Ligt moving closer to full involvement is a far better outcome than any scoreline from a private game.

title: Guardians vs White Sox predictions. Who wins Game 1 of ALDS?
description: The Guardians and White Sox begin the ALDS with Game 1 on Saturday, Oct. 3 at 1 p.m. Here are our predictions for the game.
fullText:
CLEVELAND — A divisional rivalry now adds a postseason chapter.

The No. 2-seeded Guardians, who earned a bye through the AL Wild Card Series, meet the No. 6 Chicago White Sox for Game 1 of the best-of-five ALDS at 1 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 3.

Here are Guardians-White Sox Game 1 predictions from Beacon Journal sports writers Ryan Lewis and Nate Ulrich.

Lewis: The White Sox will throw an opener/bullpen game to begin the series, which can present its own challenges for a lineup, and Parker Messick will be entering his first postseason atmosphere. But being able to throw a potential Cy Young finalist and Rookie of the Year candidate gives the Guardians the upper hand, especially with their bullpen well rested. title: Bills vs. Patriots weather looks nearly perfect Sunday
description: Sunny skies, temperatures in the 60s and light winds are forecast when the Bills host the Patriots Sunday in Orchard Park.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills host their third consecutive home game of the season and conditions should once again be the autumnal ideal in Orchard Park.

The new Highmark Stadium has yet to see a game in poor weather. Sunday will be no exception, with temperatures in the mid-60s and mostly sunny skies. With the New England Patriots arriving fresh off a 35-6 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Josh Allen and the Bills will look to keep their unbeaten streak alive in near-perfect conditions.

The National Weather Service in Buffalo calls for sunny skies Sunday, a high near 68 degrees and south winds around 7 mph becoming southwest in the afternoon.

The AccuWeather forecast calls for slightly cooler temperatures — 65 degrees rising to just 66 degrees — but expects the same mostly sunny skies and no precipitation. Winds are predicted to be a bit more active at 10 mph.

The 3-0 Bills were favored by about a touchdown over the 1-2 New England Patriots as of Friday evening. MVP runner-up Drake Maye has already been responsible for seven turnovers in the young season. The over/under is set at 49.5 points, which might require heavy lifting by a Bills offense leading the league at 33.7 points per game; the Patriots are tied for a league-worst 12 points per game.

With mild temperatures, winds at or near the NFL-standard 7 mph and no precipitation in the forecast, weather isn't expected to affect the outcome of this rivalry game.

The New England Patriots lead the all-time series against the Buffalo Bills, 80-52-1. Buffalo won their last matchup, 35-31, on Dec. 14, 2025 in Foxboro behind 28 second-half points.

The Bills and Patriots play Sunday, Oct. 4 at 1 p.m. at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park. The game will be broadcast on CBS affiliates, including WROC Channel 8 in Rochester. Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker will call the game with sideline reporter Evan Washburn.

title: Maxx Crosby: Vegas is a different type of city, we have to earn home-field advantage
description: "We're new to this city and we have to win. The fans come out, they want to see a winner. We have to earn that," Crosby said.
fullText:
The Raiders haven't had a lot of success since moving to Las Vegas in 2020, but things may be changing. The Raiders are 3-0, on Sunday they host the 3-0 Chiefs, and Maxx Crosby says now is the time to show what kind of home-field advantage Allegiant Stadium can provide.

Crosby said that unlike Oakland and Los Angeles, where the rabid fans of the Black Hole were legendary, Vegas is a city where the Raiders are going to need to develop a fan base that isn't yet so invested in the team.

"We're gonna need the fans at full effect, and that's all season," Crosby said. "We have to earn our stadium, and having the fans here. In Oakland it's built in, fans are going to show up, it's going to be Silver and Black. L.A. is the same thing. But Vegas is a different type of city. We're new to this city and we have to win. The fans come out, they want to see a winner. We have to earn that."

Crosby thinks winning comes first and the home-field advantage follows.

"We take it one day at a time and keep earning the respect, and love and passion for the fans. We know the fans have it, to fill that stadium every Sunday with Silver and Black, we've got to continue winning and keep putting a great product out there for the fans," Crosby said.

If the Raiders beat the Chiefs on Sunday, a whole lot of Las Vegas fans will be buying in.

title: Antonelli makes stark Verstappen admission after Mercedes falls short
description: Kimi Antonelli gave credit to pole-sitter Max Verstappen in Malaysia, simply admitting that the Dutchman was too quick for him to mount a challenge for pole position today. The Italian headed into Q3 with only one attempt at his disposal after having a lap time deleted for exceeding track limits in Q2, leaving him without the opportunity for another final push like the other drivers.
fullText:
Kimi Antonelli gave credit to pole-sitter Max Verstappen in Malaysia, simply admitting that the Dutchman was too quick for him to mount a challenge for pole position today.

The Italian headed into Q3 with only one attempt at his disposal after having a lap time deleted for exceeding track limits in Q2, leaving him without the opportunity for another final push like the other drivers. Although Verstappen ultimately proved untouchable, the championship leader still qualified four positions ahead of his title rival and teammate, who also appeared well off the pace.

Speaking to GPblog among other media after qualifying, the Italian admitted that a track-limits mistake cost him the chance to start higher up the grid, although he conceded that Verstappen's pace was ultimately beyond his reach.

"I did a mistake with the track limit. I understeered off the track, but I think with a clean qualifying, probably P2, maybe P3 on the road, but not P1. Max was a bit too quick for us today."

Antonelli also stressed that Mercedes still has plenty to learn about its new package, with Sepang's rough surface and extreme temperatures making it particularly difficult to properly assess the upgrades. Despite those challenges, he remains confident that the team will have an opportunity to fight at the front in the race.

"I think there's a lot of learning that we need to make about this package. I think the track doesn't help as well because the tarmac is so rough and it's so hot that tires are out of the windows after two corners. So we're just sliding around and it's making our life difficult to understand this package. We have a big opportunity tomorrow to score good points to hopefully even fight for the win, and I'll do my best."

Speaking about the new package and why it has so far failed to deliver the results Mercedes had hoped for, Antonelli explained that the upgrades have changed the car's operating window, leaving the team with more work to do to understand where it can extract the most performance.

"With this new package, obviously, the window of the way the car operates is different. So I think we're trying to understand in which window the car performs at its best, in the high-speed corner and low-speed corner."

The Italian pointed to Mercedes' encouraging pace through the high-speed sections as one of the main positives from the weekend, but admitted that the car has struggled considerably 

"I think our high-speed performance has been very strong this weekend. We were very quick in the high speed, but in the low speed where we lacked. So I think overall, we need to understand why and try to move on and improve."

Verstappen believes Red Bull's recent progress has come from a combination of a better understanding of the RB22 andan upgrade package that has successfully addressed some of the weaknesses that had previously limited the car. The Dutchman explained that the new parts have delivered the expected gains, improving both outright lap time and the overall balance of the car.

Those improvements have been particularly valuable at Sepang, where the high temperatures make stability and predictability even more important. With the tyres highly sensitive to changes in balance, having a more connected car has allowed Red Bull to extract additional performance, an area in which Verstappen feels the team has made noticeable progress over the latest race weekend.

The result was Verstappen's first pole position of the season and a return to a familiar scenario at the front of the grid. He will start alongside Lewis Hamilton, with the two former title rivals sharing the front row once again after producing plenty of action from similar starting positions in the past.

title: Ducks "survive" season opener in Vegas, turning 4-goal lead into 1-goal win
description: On the strength of Leo Carlsson, the top line and Lukáš Dostál, Anaheim earned a 4-0 lead in the first 30 minutes, but Vegas swung momentum and forced the Ducks to hold on in 3-goal third period.
fullText:
LAS VEGAS – Despite embarking on a newly expanded 84-game season, the Anaheim Ducks were the 31st team of the NHL's 32 to open up the 2026-27 season on Friday, but they made the wait well worth it.

Anaheim scored three goals in a 2:36 span across the first and second periods and charged out to a 4-0 lead to cruise in their season opener over the Vegas Golden Knights at T-Mobile Arena.

Beckett Sennecke scored the first goal of the season on an all-world stretch feed from Leo Carlsson, who collected two points on the night. Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott scored on tips, and Carlsson cleaned up a rebound off the rush for the 4-0 lead in the second period.

Eleven different Ducks found the scoresheet against the team that ended their first Stanley Cup playoff appearance in eight seasons back in May.

Vegas quickly clawed back and swung momentum with two goals in 1:29 the third period, as Shea Theodore's goal was upheld on review, and Tomas Hertl scored on the ensuing power play for Anaheim's failed offside challenge.

"They said the puck was out, and that's what we were concerned about," Joel Quenneville said, "but they said they tagged up. We got a look at it. I hadn't looked at that part of it. My fault."

Vegas cut the deficit to just one goal with 2:50 remaining, and despite a desperation scramble sequence in the final 30 seconds, the Ducks survived.

"First game of the season. Get out with a win," Carlsson said. "A little bit tighter than we wanted at the end. We expected a push, but we won the game, so it's good."

Anaheim (1-0-0, 2 points) returns to Orange County for the home opener on Sunday against former captain Radko Gudas and the Florida Panthers to kick off a two-game home set.

Two-thirds of Anaheim's first line made total sense on paper when it first took to the practice ice on Wednesday. No. 1 center Leo Carlsson was flanked by leading goal-scorer Cutter Gauthier, as the Ducks went to their top guns for the top line.

Would Beckett Sennecke join them to totally load up? Maybe first-round pick Nikita Klepov would make his debut, after sliding in seamlessly during the preseason?

Neither got the nod, as new addition AJ Greer made his surprise appearance on the line, and the next day and into Friday's morning skate and season opener.

Greer made his name as a grinder with the Florida Panthers, and while he hit career highs while playing up in the line-up for an injury-decimated Panthers squad last season, he'd been generally thought to be a bottom-six addition for Anaheim.

While praising Greer's energy and inside grit, even the line's architect Joel Quenneville wasn't totally sure what he had made."I'm curious to see how he's gonna handle it as well," Quenneville said Friday morning.

Well, what Quenneville put together was Anaheim's best line of the night, as the trio dominated early shifts, earned 72.66% of expected goals at five-on-five and each collected a point in their first game of the season.

Greer took on the dirty work on the forecheck, while Carlsson and Gauthier used the space to open up their speed for more chances and their own forecheck battles.

"I can keep up with them and create space for them off the rush," Greer said. "They've got a lot of poise with the puck, great IQ. Cutter's got an amazing shot. Leo's got amazing hands and can make a play through anything. So, I go to the net. I got to create space for them and make sure that I'm doing my role and playing physical."

Carlsson made a spectacular play without his linemates to end the first period. He fired a tape-to-tape outlet pass from his own face-off dot to the far blue line past all five Golden Knights on the ice to spring a Beckett Sennecke breakaway.

"I was so tired, so I didn't really think much," Carlsson said. "Just saw him all alone. Just tried to pass it as hard as I could, and it ended up being perfect."

Later in the second period with a 3-0 lead, Gauthier pounced on a turnover at center ice and pushed the pace with Greer on a two-on-one. Gauthier took the shot, which was stopped, and Greer followed up on the rebound, which required a sprawling save from the Vegas netminder.

However, the goalie slid out of his crease, and with the puck sitting at the top of the blue paint, Carlsson swooped in to slam home Anaheim's fourth of the night.

🚨 Sennecke 🚨

What a feed by Leo and Becks goes bar down!
We lead 1-0. #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/idtJFoG28f

While the Ducks bolted out on the strength of their offensive determination, the four-goal lead came in tandem with a foundational performance in net from Lukáš Dostál.

After a subpar regular season by Dostál's standards and a playoffs he'd like to put behind him, Dostál set the tone for Anaheim early.

The Czech Olympian made a humongous post-to-post stop on the Ducks' first penalty kill of the game, and ahead of Carlsson's outlet pass for Sennecke's goal, Dostál slammed the door shut on another jam play into the crease.

"He's so good," Carlsson said. "He keeps us in games every time. Huge shout for him."

Vegas had generated just over 1.6 expected goals in all situations through two periods, where Dostál had made 17 saves to that point to keep the Knights off the board.

For his heroics, Dostál credited the young blue line in front of him."I'm proud of our group, because I thought our guys were unbelievable," Dostál said. "I honestly felt like we played a simple game. We simplified. We didn't make anything harder than we had to."

However, Anaheim and Dostál's 163-game search for their first shutouts since the season opener of the 2024-25 season (Oct. 12, 2024) would continue, as Vegas got on the board early in the third period.

Shea Theodore would beat Dostál cleanly through some bodies for the first, and after the failed offside challenge, Tomas Hertl scored on some lax netfront defense on the ensuing power play.

With three minutes to go, Dostál couldn't cover a puck that Brandon Bowman would pot to cut the lead to one, but the 26-year-old came up when it counted in the final minute.

Vegas got several whacks in a desperate goalmouth scramble in the last 30 seconds of the game, but Anaheim's shot blockers and Dostál made the lead hold up for the first win of the season.

"One of those where we survive," Dostál said.

Just one day after inking a six-year, $7.2 million-per-season deal that had many outside of Anaheim asking, "who is Tristan Luneau," the 22-year-old Ducks blue-liner played a career-high 26:58 of ice time, was not on the ice for a goal against and Anaheim earned 58.3% of the expected goals while Luneau was on the ice at five-on-five. The NHL will get to know Luneau soon enough.

Noah Warren made his NHL debut and earned his first NHL point on a shot tipped in by Alex Killorn early in the second period. Warren played just 9:33 of ice time, but Anaheim earned 78.23% of the expected goals at five-on-five with Warren on the ice. "It's a dream come true," Warren said Friday morning. "I feel proud of myself, and I think I'm ready."

Judd Caulfield also made his NHL debut on Friday and played 13:17 of ice time in a fourth-line role.

Sennecke scored for the second consecutive season opener, making him just the fourth player in Ducks history to do so following Rickard Rakell, Andrew Cogliano and Rob Niedermayer

title: Green Bay Packers could make surprising Keisean Nixon decision after rough start to the season
description: The Green Bay Packers remain focused on adding talent, but their approach does not rule out moving players when the right offer comes along. That could put Keisean Nixon’s future with the team in question. Nixon has struggled through the opening weeks of the 2026 season, and Zachary Rottman of FanSided believes Green Bay’s current [...]
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers remain focused on adding talent, but their approach does not rule out moving players when the right offer comes along. That could put Keisean Nixon's future with the team in question. Nixon has struggled through the opening weeks of the 2026 season, and Zachary Rottman of FanSided believes Green Bay's current situation could eventually result in the Packers moving on from the veteran.

"Trading Nixon right now is probably a non-starter, but he's on an expiring contract, and I'm not sold on the Packers ever turning things around," wrote the NFL insider.

"If they fall out of contention, it'd make sense for all parties for Nixon to get a fresh start."

Rottman identified the Detroit Lions and Pittsburgh Steelers as potential destinations for Nixon. Detroit previously pursued a trade for Joey Porter Jr. without getting a deal done, while Pittsburgh recently moved on from Porter. With both teams needing help at cornerback, Nixon could emerge as an option for either club.

The possibility of Green Bay moving on from Nixon was already emerging before the 2026 season began. The Packers added Benjamin St. Juste during free agency and then used a second round pick on Brandon Cisse, giving the team two additional options at cornerback.

Nixon has struggled more than ever during the opening stretch of the 2026 season. PFF has given him a 53.5 overall grade and a 49.8 mark in coverage. Since taking on a full time starting role in Green Bay, his previous career lows were a 60 overall grade and a 60.4 coverage grade.

A trade would therefore come with the Packers selling at a low point, although Nixon is entering the final season of the three year, $18 million extension he signed in 2024.

title: Liverpool could be set for Michael Olise boost after Bayern Munich talks
description: Michael Olise to Liverpool? Bayern Contract Twist Could Open the DoorLiverpool’s long-term interest in Michael Olise may have received a significant lift, with fresh reporting from Christian Falk su...
fullText:
Liverpool's long-term interest in Michael Olise may have received a significant lift, with fresh reporting from Christian Falk suggesting Bayern Munich are considering an unusual contractual route to secure the France international's future.

The situation is straightforward in broad terms. Liverpool have been in the market for a high-end right-sided attacker since Mohamed Salah's summer departure. That gap has remained obvious. Recruitment options at the very top level were limited and, as a result, no direct replacement arrived. Michael Olise has long stood out as one of the few players capable of filling that role at elite level.

Until now, Bayern's position has appeared firm. Olise is tied to a deal until 2029 and there has been little realistic expectation of movement in 2026. Liverpool, like any other interested club, would have known that Bayern held all the leverage.

That is where this latest development becomes relevant. Bayern are understood to want Olise on improved terms, while recognising the market pressure around a player of his quality. The reported solution is the possible inclusion of a release clause, something that would represent a notable concession from the Bundesliga champions.

From Bayern's perspective, it would protect value. Rather than risk a scenario in which Olise edges closer to the final stages of his deal and his market price starts to fall, they could lock in both security and a premium exit route. The figure being discussed is €200m, which underlines both the player's status and Bayern's determination to remain in control.

For Liverpool, the key point is less about the headline number and more about the principle. A release clause changes the conversation. It creates a defined pathway, even if that pathway is expensive. Clubs can plan around a mechanism like that. They can assess timing, structure and whether there is any room to negotiate beneath the clause with the selling side.

There is no suggestion a deal is close, and there would be major financial considerations around any move of this scale. Even so, clarity matters. If Olise becomes a player with a formal exit condition in his contract, Liverpool would know exactly where they stand.

That is why this update feels important. It does not place Liverpool on the brink of signing Olise, but it does move the story from fantasy to framework. Bayern would still be seeking an enormous fee, and any pursuit would likely become one of the biggest transfer discussions in Europe.

Olise remains one of the most gifted attacking players available to the top end of the market. If Liverpool are serious about addressing the right wing with a statement signing, this is the sort of opening they will monitor very closely over the months ahead.

From a Liverpool supporter's perspective, this is exactly the kind of report that sparks hope, even if the numbers involved are eye-watering. Olise looks like the calibre of player you wait for, the sort of attacker who can change the dynamic of a title-chasing side and give the right flank genuine star quality again.

There is also a wider point here. Under Andoni Iraola, Liverpool need top-level wide players who can create chaos in one-v-one situations, carry a scoring threat and operate under intense pressure. Olise ticks every one of those boxes. He has composure, imagination and end product, and those traits are hard to find at the very highest level.

No supporter should assume this would be simple. Bayern rarely make life easy in the market and €200m is clearly an extraordinary valuation. Even so, if a clause is inserted, there is at least a route. That matters. Liverpool can budget, strategise and decide whether this is the marquee move worth building towards.

For fans, that is enough to dream. If the club believe Olise is the standout option to reshape the attack, then this development feels like the first genuine sign that the door might open, however slightly.

title: NFL insider reveals why the Green Bay Packers remain “At least a tier below” NFL heavyweights
description: The Green Bay Packers have plenty of season left to turn things around, but their 1-2 record has put them at the bottom of the NFC North. Matt LaFleur’s men have already dropped a divisional matchup to the 3-0 Minnesota Vikings. The team will try to even its record Sunday when it travels to face [...]
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers have plenty of season left to turn things around, but their 1-2 record has put them at the bottom of the NFC North. Matt LaFleur's men have already dropped a divisional matchup to the 3-0 Minnesota Vikings. The team will try to even its record Sunday when it travels to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 4.

Bleacher Report's Brad Gagnon recently summed up September for every NFL team in a single sentence. His assessment of the Green Bay Packers, however, painted a less than encouraging picture of their opening month.

"They've played three teams that didn't make the playoffs in 2025 but have yet to win a game in regulation, proving that Green Bay remains at least a tier below true heavyweight status," wrote the NFL insider.

Green Bay appeared to be in control after taking a 22-10 lead against Minnesota in the opener, but the Vikings completely took over from there. Minnesota scored 29 consecutive points to secure a 39-22 comeback victory. The Packers responded the following week by earning their first win of the year, edging the New York Jets 20-17 in overtime.

The Packers could not carry that momentum into Week 3, suffering a lopsided 35-14 defeat against the Atlanta Falcons in its home opener. The Packers struggled to slow Atlanta throughout the afternoon, allowing the Falcons to rack up nearly 500 total yards, including 242 rushing yards.

Gagnon's assessment stings because it's accurate. The Packers have faced winnable matchups and squandered opportunities, including a collapse against Minnesota and a home loss to Atlanta that revealed their defensive vulnerabilities. Heading to Tampa Bay at 1-2 adds urgency to a season that looked promising just weeks ago.

LaFleur's team can't afford another divisional-round exit, and the current trajectory suggests they're trending toward missing the playoffs entirely. The Buccaneers present a chance to salvage September, but Green Bay needs more than just one win. They need to prove they can compete with playoff contenders and execute at a consistent level.

title: Solberg piles pressure on Evans in WRC title race
description: Elfyn Evans' hopes of claiming a first World Rally Championship title are in the balance after another strong morning for rival Oliver Solberg in Sardinia.
fullText:
Elfyn Evans' hopes of claiming a first World Rally Championship (WRC) crown are hanging by a thread after rival Oliver Solberg took the lead in the title-deciding Rally Italia Sardegna.

Solberg was again the fastest driver across Saturday morning's three stages, leapfrogging the overnight top two, Hyundai pair Thierry Neuville and Adrien Fourmaux.

The 25-year-old Swede leads Neuville by 2.7 seconds, while Evans lies in sixth place, one minute and 57.7 seconds behind the new rally leader.

The Welshman had taken a 17-point lead into the final round of the season, but on current positions that gap would be reduced to four.

With up to 10 points available as Sunday bonuses, and given Solberg's flying form in Sardinia, that puts him as the favourite to claim a maiden world title rather than his Toyota team-mate.

"A bit out of my control, I feel, with the road cleaning so much," said Welshman Evans when asked about the title race after stage 10.

"[We're] not realistically going to catch anybody in front, got to stay clean for now."

The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory

Evans on track for WRC title despite tough day

Eight-time world champion Sebastien Ogier lies third, Fourmaux fourth and Sami Pajari, who could also still win the WRC title, in fifth position.

The Finn is 42.2 seconds ahead of Evans and co-driver Scott Martin, who were again unable to match the fastest times on Saturday despite no longer facing the challenge of being the first car out on loose gravel surfaces.

Trailing 51.7 seconds behind Evans in seventh place is Josh McErlean, who lost time on stage 10 with a half-spin to avoid a tree.

McErlean's M-Sport Ford team-mate and fellow Irishman Jon Armstrong is ninth.

Evans will guarantee himself a first WRC title if he collects 19 points from the maximum 35 available to any one driver over a rally weekend.

He has averaged 19.2 points per event this season.

The winner of the rally will collect 25 points, with 17 for second, 15 for third and so on down to one for 10th place.

A further five, four, three, two and one points are available for the five quickest drivers over Sunday's four stages, with the same bonuses awarded for the fastest times on the final Power Stage.

That means any of these five scenarios would guarantee Evans his first world title.

Second overall plus at least two Sunday bonus points

Third overall plus at least four bonus points

Fourth overall plus at least seven bonus points

Fifth overall plus at least nine bonus points

If, on the other hand, Evans fails to collect 19 points this weekend, that does not mean his dream is over, but it does open the door for his rivals.

Pajari must outscore championship leader Evans by at least 18 points - in addition to gaining four more than Solberg - to take the title.

If the Finnish driver - who has won three of the past four rallies - were to take the maximum 35 points, that would mean Evans could score no more than 18.

Those returns would see the Toyota pair tied on 248 points and make Pajari champion by virtue of four rally victories this season compared to the Welshman's two.

Solberg, winner of the previous rally in Chile, needs to score at least 22 points more than Evans and five more than Pajari to take the title.

If he were to enjoy a maximum 35-point weekend and Evans picked up 15, the pair would be level on 244 points, making the Swede world champion on countback with three rally victories.

The rally continues with a further 13 stages before the winner - and the 2026 World Rally champion - is crowned on Sunday.

title: Exeter sign former Lincoln winger Scully
description: Exeter City sign ex-Lincoln City and Wigan winger Anthony Scully on a deal until the end of the season.
fullText:
Exeter City have signed ex-Lincoln City and Wigan winger Anthony Scully on a deal until the end of the season.

The 27-year-old was a free agent after spending last season with Shrewsbury Town and has been training with the PFA camp all summer.

Scully was a key player for Lincoln, scoring 37 goals in 106 games, before leaving in 2022 and manager Matt Taylor is confident he can get back to his best.

"Anthony is a player we've come across before and I've got strong memories of his energy, his ability on the ball and his enthusiasm for attacking moments," Taylor said.

"He's 27, has a strong pedigree and still has a lot to offer.

"He had other opportunities available to him, but he sees this as a good fit for himself, as much as we see it as a good fit for him. I'm delighted he's chosen to come here and hopefully we can help him reach his peak."

title: Jon Morosi reveals why these Milwaukee Brewers are different ahead of October
description: The Milwaukee Brewers have established themselves as a consistent force during the regular season, but their postseason results have not always matched that success. Now, after putting together the best record in baseball, Milwaukee enters October with another opportunity to turn a dominant regular season into a deep playoff run. The Brewers set a new [...]
fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers have established themselves as a consistent force during the regular season, but their postseason results have not always matched that success. Now, after putting together the best record in baseball, Milwaukee enters October with another opportunity to turn a dominant regular season into a deep playoff run.

The Brewers set a new franchise record by winning 103 games and earned the top seed in the National League. Their reward is an NLDS matchup with the San Diego Padres, and MLB Network's Jon Morosi believes Milwaukee has a roster capable of handling the postseason test better than it has in previous years.

"It's a different @Brewers team, a better Brewers team."@jonmorosi examines Milwaukee's strengths and how their infusion of young talent has added another element to their World Series chances. pic.twitter.com/PS6oezLIWO

— MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) October 2, 2026

"Different personnel. They have new arrivals… [Cooper] Pratt was not on the team. [Luis] Lara was not on the team… It's a different Brewers team; it's a better Brewers team," commented the MLB insider.

"But can we get a five-game series between the Padres and Brewers? So many stars in this series."

Morosi specifically pointed to Garrett Mitchell and David Hamilton as examples of the added depth Milwaukee can bring into October. His point centers on the changes to the Brewers' roster, with this postseason group offering a different mix of players than the teams that came up short in previous years.

Jacob Misiorowski could be one of the biggest factors shaping Milwaukee's postseason outlook. After another year of development, the right hander has emerged as an NL Cy Young favorite while leading MLB with a 1.80 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and 252 strikeouts. Having a pitcher produce at that level gives the Brewers a major weapon as they look to take control of the series early.

Milwaukee took a step forward last postseason by getting past the Chicago Cubs in the NLDS. However, the Los Angeles Dodgers ended the Brewers' run in the NLCS with a sweep, showing that Milwaukee still had ground to make up against the National League's top competition.

Now, Milwaukee will have to show that progress against the San Diego Padres.
