fullText:
Nebraska refuses to go away in the recruitment of Ruston (La.) four-star tight end Ahmad Hudson. According to HuskerOnline, the standout LSU commit is returning to Lincoln for another visit this weekend.

The 6-foot-6, 245-pounder is expected back at Memorial Stadium as the Huskers host Maryland. It's Hudson's first visit to Nebraska since he took an official visit back in June and his fifth trip to the Big Ten program overall. LSU has held his commitment since May 3.

$19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage

Hudson is the No. 37 overall prospect and No. 2 TE in the 2027 cycle, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings, a weighted average that utilizes all major recruiting media companies. He's also the No. 4 prospect in The Boot.

He also doubles as a blue-chip basketball prospect (No. 24 NATL., No. 5 center) and intends on playing both sports at the college level. Nebraska has long been running second in his recruitment, but it continues to give LSU a run for its money. Getting a visit this late in the process is notable for head coach Matt Rhule and Co.

LSU did get Hudson back to Baton Rouge twice last month. His mother, Britt Hassen, continued to speak highly of the Tigers when discussing Hudson's recruitment with Rivals' Sam Spiegelman on Sept. 14:

"Everything is going great," Hassen said after her family's visit back to Tiger Stadium. "It's always exciting to get to Baton Rouge to enjoy the experience of Death Valley. The Coaches are always excited to see the boys."

"I think the biggest thing has been how genuine and consistent they've been with both Ahmad and Branson," she continued on the visit. "The coaches and JR (Belton) have made an effort to build relationships with them beyond just football, and as a mom, I think that naturally helps them feel comfortable and welcomed whenever they're back at LSU."

Despite LSU doing all it can to keep Hudson in the fold, he's now reportedly making the trip back to the Midwest this weekend. Nebraska five-star quarterback commit Trae Taylor has been an elite player recruiter and he's been after Hudson for a long time.

"Just how they have a family feeling," Hudson previously told Rivals about what interests him in Lincoln. "Being at Nebraska feels like I'm in Ruston, Louisiana. What excites me is how they get the ball to the tight end in multiple ways. And they told me they would use me in a whole bunch of ways that I like."

Hudson is the top-ranked commit in LSU's 2027 class — which ranks 10th nationally, per the Rivals Industry Team Recruiting Rankings. Nebraska currently has the No. 18 class, but it would shoot up the rankings if it were able to flip Hudson away from the Tigers.

title: Dodgers could take advantage of run-down Braves, top pitcher in NLDS
description: Five weeks ago, Chris Sale was a problem for the Dodgers. In a 1-0 win for the Braves at Truist Park, Sale pitched a complete-game shutout, striking out 11 batters...
fullText:
Five weeks ago, Chris Sale was a problem for the Dodgers.

In a 1-0 win for the Braves at Truist Park, Sale pitched a complete-game shutout, striking out 11 batters over nine innings.

But the Dodgers won't see Sale on the mound at Dodger Stadium on Saturday in Game 1 of their National League Division Series.

They might not see him on Sunday in Game 2, either.

Because Braves manager Walt Weiss made the baffling decision to turn to Sale with a four-run lead to close out the deciding game of an NL Wild Card Series against the Phillies, there's a chance the Dodgers won't have to face the former Cy Young Award winner until the third game of the best-of-five series.

"A lot's going to depend on how Chris feels," Weiss said.

With one of the top bullpens in baseball, the NL East champion Braves present a real threat to the Dodgers on paper.

Reality won't be nearly as dramatic.

Defeating the Phillies came at an extreme cost for the Braves, who enter this series looking more like cannon fodder than a realistic challenger.

"The Phillies series took a lot out of us, as far as our pitching," Weiss said.

That series stretched to three games, with the games played on consecutive days. Closer Raisel Iglesias, fireballer Didier Fuentes and left-hander Dylan Lee pitched on Tuesday and Wednesday, with Fuentes returning to pitch again in the series finale.

In their bullpen game on Thursday, the Braves used six pitchers, including Sale, who was entrusted to take down the last four outs of a four-run game two days after he pitched 6 ⅓ innings in a Game 1 win.

The way the Braves used their relievers in the wild-card matchup will handicap a bullpen that was one of the best of baseball in the regular season.

"The advantage for us is we have an opportunity to not let their pitching staff come up for air," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.

In fact, with Weiss saying that sidelined starters Martin Perez and Bryce Elder won't return in this round, the Braves could have to resort to bullpen games in Games 1 and 2.

In retrospect, Sale was more than a proverbial nail in the coffin for the Phillies — he was closer to an atomic bomb. But if Sale's eighth-inning entrance detonated the minuscule chances of a Phillies comeback, it might have also nuked the Braves' attempt to upset the Dodgers.

If Sale doesn't pitch until Game 3, he will be limited to one start in the NLDS. So will Tyler Mahle, the only other usable starting pitcher on the Braves' roster.

But say Sale can pitch by Sunday. What will the 37-year-old Sale look like after pitching in relief on Thursday? In that game, Sale threw four pitches in the eighth inning, sat on the bench for a half-inning, then returned to the mound to throw 17 more pitches.

Pitching in Game 2 would make Sale available to start Game 5 on four days' rest, but, again, how will Sale look at that point? If Sale takes the mound for a hypothetical fifth game, he would be starting opposite Tarik Skubal, who would be pitching on five days' rest.

Don't begrudge the Dodgers for this advantage. They earned it by securing one of the NL's top two seeds, which earned them a bye in the wild-card round.

In 2021, the Dodgers won a then-franchise-record 106 games but had to play in a winner-take-all wild-card game because they were edged for the NL West title by the Giants. After beating the Cardinals on a walk-off home run in the wild-card game, the Dodgers were pushed to five games by the Giants in the NLDS. Max Scherzer closed out the last game of the NLDS, which affected him in the next round against the Braves. Scherzer lasted only 4 ⅓ innings in his Game 2 start and had to be scratched from his Game 6 assignment.

The record shows the Dodgers were eliminated by the Braves that year, but the truth was the damage they sustained in the Giants series is what ended their postseason run.

This time, the Dodgers are on the other side of the equation.

title: Mizzou Soccer earns first conference point against Arkansas
description: Taryn Chance’s first goal as a Tiger led them to a 1-1 draw
fullText:
Missouri women's soccer earned its first SEC point of the season Friday night, as Taryn Chance's equalizer in the 72nd minute salvaged a 1-1 draw at Razorback Field. The result snapped the Tigers' four-match losing streak to open conference play.

Missouri trailed for only about seven minutes, but it spent most of the second half under pressure from the Razorbacks, who outshot the Tigers 10-7 after the break. Goalkeeper Riley Wilkerson made five saves, three of them in the second half, to keep the game within reach.

Neither team scored in a first half that was largely even. The Tigers held an 8-7 edge in shots, with Lana Adams taking five of the Tigers' 15 total attempts. Mia Yang forced a save from Arkansas goalkeeper Keegan Smith in the 24th minute, and Adams and Landis Canada each put shots on target before halftime, but the Tigers went to the break scoreless.

The Razorbacks broke through in the 65th minute. Natalie Wagner set up Vailana Tu'ua, who got behind the Missouri defense and finished by placing the ball into the top right corner. Tu'ua led all players with four shots, three on target.

Missouri answered quickly. In the 72nd minute, Alyssa Bryant sent a shot toward the bottom center of the net that was saved, and Chance put away the follow-up with a swooping left-footed shot that beat the keeper across the goal and nestled into the side netting.

A Purdue transfer who joined the Tigers this year, Chance came on in the 29th minute for Adams and played 61 minutes. The goal, the first of her Missouri career, was her only shot of the game.

The Tigers had chances to win it. Emily Derucki, Canada and McKenna Moran each got shots away late, but Arkansas blocked or missed all three. At the other end, Wilkerson turned away Tu'ua in the 88th minute and Kennedy Ball in the 89th. Arkansas won a corner in the final seconds, and officials reviewed the play for a possible goal, but the draw stood.

Missouri was out-cornered 9-3 and outshot 17-15 overall, but they matched Arkansas with six shots on goal apiece.

The game turned physical late. Mia Devrouax received a yellow card for unsporting behavior in the 85th minute, and Arkansas was shown a team yellow for unsporting behavior in the 88th. Missouri committed six fouls to Arkansas' eight.

The draw was the Tigers' first SEC point since a draw with Auburn on Oct. 24 last season. Coming against a ranked Arkansas side, it also snapped an 11-match losing streak.

The result completed a two-match SEC road trip. The Tigers now return home to face No. 3 Vanderbilt in Columbia on Friday, Oct. 9.

title: Former New Orleans Pelicans Draft Pick Jordan Hawkins Released By Grizzlies
description: Former New Orleans Pelicans lottery pick Jordan Hawkins was released by the Memphis Grizzlies in a mutual decision.
fullText:
The New Orleans Pelicans recently moved on from guard Jordan Hawkins, trading him, along with Micah Peavy and some draft capital, to the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

This was a monetary move for the Pelicans, and seemingly just a move for Peavy and the picks for the Grizzlies, as they decided to release Hawkins on Friday night, per ESPN's Shams Charania. It was a mutual decision, though, and it could end up being to the benefit of Hawkins.

The former lottery pick had fallen on hard times over the past couple of seasons in New Orleans. This past season, over 51 appearances, Hawkins had posted just 5.1 points, 1.7 rebounds and 0.8 assists on 36.6/34.8/85.2 shooting splits on just 13.6 minutes per night.

Hawkins had a promising rookie season, showing some of that potential to be a sniper that he did in college, but that quickly turned into a sophomore slump. Despite Joe Dumars and co. investing in him and accepting his fourth-year option, he was basically unplayable in Year 3.

There is still talent there to be untapped, but it will take a lot of work and a different coaching style than he received with the Pelicans. It's not all his fault; he's not the only player who didn't develop under the previous regime, but there is plenty he has to change as well.

New Orleans ended up needing his money to sign Bennedict Mathurin, and will now take a chance on Johnson instead, another project piece guard. Johnson is both cheaper and younger, at least.

Hopefully, Hawkins can land somewhere that knows what to do with him and get his career back on the right track.

title: Red Wings Waste Anton Johansson’s Debut in Shutout Loss
description: Detroit was shut out 2-0 on opening night despite outshooting the Rangers. #RedWings
fullText:
Red Wings opening night ended with 22 shots, zero goals, and a building that made sure the front office heard about it. The Detroit Red Wings lost 2-0 to the New York Rangers on Friday at Little Caesars Arena, wasting a steady NHL debut from rookie defenseman Anton Johansson. Detroit outshot New York 22-21 and still could not solve Rangers goaltender Dylan Garand, who stopped all 22 for the shutout. There were ups and downs, but on the whole it was a decent showing that had nothing to show for it.

New York looked like the team with two games already behind it, and it controlled the pace early. Nate Danielson took a holding penalty 3:31 into the first period, and the Rangers needed less than two minutes of it. Sean Durzi beat John Gibson with a slap shot at 5:12, with Gabe Perreault and Will Cuylle picking up the assists. Durzi landed in New York on July 1 as the centerpiece of the Vincent Trocheck trade with the Utah Mammoth, a deal that also sent prospect Cole Beaudoin and a 2027 third-round pick to the Rangers.

It got chippy 26 seconds later. Michael Rasmussen took a roughing penalty in an after-whistle scrum, and Keegan Kolesar and Joe Veleno, a former Red Wing now in New York, traded unsportsmanlike conduct minors that canceled each other out. Rasmussen's penalty put the Rangers back on the power play anyway. Durzi appeared to score again later in the period, but Detroit challenged for offside and the goal came off the board.

Detroit closed the shot gap in the back half of the period. Anton Johansson put a snap shot just over the crossbar, Michael Brandsegg-Nygard worked a chance of his own, and Marco Kasper was turned aside by Garand. Alberts Smits went off for cross-checking at 12:38, which handed the Red Wings the first power play of their season. They did not score on it.

The second period was Detroit's best, and the Red Wings looked far more poised than they had in the first. Durzi tripped J.T. Compher 47 seconds in, which gave Detroit its second power play of the night. That one came up empty too. The Red Wings finished the game 0-for-2 with the extra man; New York went 1-for-4.

Kasper had seen enough of Durzi's antics by 12:13, and the two dropped the gloves and each took a five-minute fighting major. Kasper has always worked for everything on the ice, and it was good to see. At the same stoppage Axel Sandin-Pellikka was called for hooking, which put New York on its third power play of the game, and Gibson made the saves that kept the deficit at one. Kasper otherwise led Detroit with four shots and won 10 of his 13 faceoffs. The period ended 1-0.

The best thing Detroit took out of the opener was the defenseman nobody had penciled in. Anton Johansson, a 22-year-old from Stockholm whom Detroit drafted 105th overall in 2022, played 19:10 in his first NHL game, third-most among Red Wings defensemen behind Moritz Seider's 25:16 and Justin Faulk's 21:29. He was handed the second pair alongside Faulk, a job that opened up with Simon Edvinsson still unsigned. Johansson finished even with a block and a hit, had the crossbar chance in the first, and is showing he deserves that spot.

Detroit started the third strongly until Faulk went off for slashing 1:28 in. The Red Wings killed the penalty and then drifted, though the team never fully collapsed and came back together as the period went on. Both sides defended well through the middle of it and the chances thinned out. Lucas Raymond carried the puck up ice in the final minutes and dropped a New York defender with a deke in the corner, which was about as close as Detroit came. Eeli Tolvanen sealed it into the empty net at 18:44, with Tye Kartye and Adam Fox credited on the assists, and New York had its 2-0 win.

The crowd was the other story. Dylan Larkin was met with loud boos, and "Sell the team" chants went up more than once. None of that was a surprise, and it should put real pressure on the front office. Garand, Durzi and Tolvanen took the three stars. All three were Rangers.

title: Carl Albert football breaks Bixby's 11-man Oklahoma winning streak record
description: Carl Albert owns the record for most football state titles in Oklahoma and now own's the state's longest 11-man win streak.
fullText:
Winning is nothing new for the Carl Albert (OK) Titans.

They've won more state championships than any other team in Oklahoma's history (20), including four straight. On Friday night, Oct. 2, they added another accomplishment to the program's illustrious history.

With a 41-6 win over Noble (OK), the Titans now own the state's longest active win streak of 59 games in a row. They snapped Bixby's streak of 58 that went from 2018-2022.

The Titans also have the longest active win streak in the country following Garden City's (NY) 21-14 loss to Massapequa (NY) on Monday night and Sheridan's (WY) 38-0 loss to Natrona County (WY) last Friday.

Carl Albert's current streak began with a 45-2 win over Elk City (OK) on September 16, 2022. The Titans started the 2022 season 1-2 and their last loss came to Muskogee (OK) by a score of 35-28.

What followed that Muskogee loss was 11 consecutive wins to close out the 2022 season and the program's 16th state championship. They followed up that season with three straight seasons where they finished 14-0 and claimed three more state championships.

The streak has been threatened at times, particularly this season.

Carl Albert opened its season with two of its wins coming by 12 points or less. The last two weeks were much closer as they held off Del City (OK) 31-28 and then kicked a game-winning field goal in the final minute last week to beat Guthrie (OK) 17-16.

On Friday night, the Titans had no issues whatsoever.

Carl Albert led by seven at the end of the first quarter and by halftime that lead had ballooned to 21-0. The Titans added three more touchdowns in the third quarter and any doubt that may have entered anyone's mind before the game was quickly extinguished.

title: Nets' Nolan Traore discusses offseason work on his body, overall game
description: Brooklyn Nets guard Nolan Traore explained what his goals were for this offseason as he worked on strengthening his body and his overall game.
fullText:
NEW YORK -- Brooklyn Nets guard Nolan Traore had a rookie season where he showed what's unique about his game and also what he needs to work on to be a productive NBA player. Brooklyn had their idea of how Traore could improve from his first NBA season and he explained what he focused on so that he could be the best version of himself this year.

"I spent a lot of time in the gym during the summer, that was the main focus. It's going to help me for basketball, for sure. It was just a good thing for me," Traore said during his Media Day interview on Monday. Based on Brooklyn's training camp roster, Traore gained 10 pounds and one inch in height as he went from 180 pounds to 190 pounds and from 6-foot-3 to 6-foot-4.

"For me, it was more the physical aspect. Obviously, the shooting, too, that was kind of it. I worked a lot on it and I feel good now. I changed a few things, too. I'm just ready now for next season," Traore continued. Traore has an interesting opportunity ahead of him as he could be the starting point guard for head coach Jordi Fernandez to begin the season, but that will depend on how he performs during training camp.

Traore, 20, is coming off a 2025-26 season in which he averaged 8.9 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 3.8 assists per game while shooting 38.0% from the field and 31.8% from behind the three-point line. Traore will be competing with Mikel Brown Jr., the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, and Ben Saraf, the No. 26 pick in the 2025 draft, for the starting point guard spot and just playing time in general.

Brown is dealing with a left ankle injury so he may not be in position to gain ground in the competition while Saraf is likely going to be relegated as the third point guard and could be looking at potential G League assignments. Either way, Traore knew that he had some work to do following his rookie year and he not only knew what he had to work on, but he took it upon himself to go beyond that this offseason.

title: Special teams major factor in Port Clinton setback
description: Port Clinton suffers first setback of season at home as special teams stifle momentum.
fullText:
Trailing by seven points, Port Clinton tried to snatch the momentum with a long run from Jace Cornell on offense and a batted pass by Liam Johnson to force a punt early in the second half.

Instead, a special teams mistake allowed Vermilion to pounce on the punt and the Sailors kicked a field goal to cap the scoring in a 24-14 victory.

"Special teams is always significant," Port Clinton coach Kevin Huntley said. "We spend a lot of time on it. One play can have a major impact on the game."

Port Clinton missed a field goal after Cornell's run.

"We had an opportunity there but we didn't execute," Huntley said. "It bit us."

College football Penn State Any Joe Paterno exhibit must include failure | Opinion

In fact, Dylan Reynolds opened the scoring with a weaving 40-yard punt return for Port Clinton. Reynolds earned a little time on special teams as a freshman last season.

"When it comes down to it, special teams are a big part of the game," Reynolds said. "When my number is called — get some blocks — I can make a play."

Reynolds emerged the last two weeks, adding an 89-yard punt return for a score against Huron last week.

"We try to put guys in position to have success," Huntley said.

Port Clinton (6-1, 1-1) suffered its first setback of the season.

"We can't worry about (the conference race)," Huntley said. "We have to make the necessary corrections and play the next team."

A Vermilion touchdown pass led to a 6-6 tie in the first quarter, before Cornell ran in from 44 yards. Cornell looked to be stopped, but emerged from traffic up the sideline. Reynolds ran in a conversion.

Vermilion rushed for a score and converted as well for a 14-14 tie. Vermilion scored on its own punt return late in the second quarter.

Port Clinton's Brody Bollinger nearly intercepted a pass in the end zone before Vermiliion's field goal. Port Clinton turne the ball over on downs three times thereafter.

"We made a lot of small errors that added up," Huntley said. "We're trying to clean things up. You can't beat yourself."

title: Buchtel-Firestone football game called at halftime due to off-field fights
description: The high school football game Friday night between Buchtel and Firestone was declared over at halftime. Here's why.
fullText:
A high school football game between Akron City Series rivals was called off at halftime on Friday, Oct. 2.

Players and coaches from Buchtel and Firestone were in their respective locker rooms at Ellet's Joseph B. Yost Stadium when Akron Public Schools officials canceled the game during halftime because of fights involving spectators inside and outside of the stadium.

No players or coaches from Firestone or Buchtel were involved in the fights. Buchtel was ahead 20-0 and was declared the winner of the game.

When asked why the game was called off, Akron Public Schools Coordinator of Athletics Tom McKinnon said, "For the safety and security of everybody in the facility, it was deemed the best solution at this time was to call the game."

Several Akron Police Department cruisers and an ambulance arrived at Ellet's stadium during halftime. There were no confirmed injuries or arrests as of 10 p.m.

"There was a fight in the stands and then it just continued outside of the stadium," McKinnon said. "No players or coaches were involved."

When asked if there were conversations to clear the stadium and parking lots to play the second half and finish the game with no spectators, McKinnon said, "We just wanted to make sure everybody at this point in time cleared the stadium and the area. The safety and the security of everybody involved was the most important thing. This is why we vacated the site. The game will not be completed at a later date. The game is over."

This story is developing and will be updated.

The Akron Beacon Journal sports department can be contacted via email at bjsports@thebeaconjournal.com.

fullText:
Noa Essengue flashes vintage form with Bulls scrimmage slam dunk? appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Chicago Bulls are ready to get the season rolling. They don't want to waste any precious time, with the season starting in just a few weeks.

On Friday, they took part in a scrimmage at the Advocate Center in Chicago. The practice was lively, with plenty of highlights. One of them was Noa Essengue, who threw it down with an emphatic slam in transition.

"Down the lane with force!" the Bulls posted on their X (formerly Twitter) page.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Down the lane with force! 🔨 @NoaEssengue https://t.co/SdrZ43Qlle pic.twitter.com/6B4KJ0OaOI

— Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) October 2, 2026

Seeing Essengue on the floor in full force is a welcome sign of relief. Last year, Essengue's rookie season was halted due to a shoulder injury. He later had to undergo surgery. Altogether, Essengue played in two NBA games before joining the Windy City Bulls in the NBA G League. Before his injury, he averaged 23.0 PPG and 8.5 RPG.

Overall, Essengue endured 6 to 7 months of rehabilitation following his surgery before being cleared to take part in non-contact activities in March 2026. Then, he took part in the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas in July.

Essengue, 19, hails from France and is still waiting to play a full NBA season. At the same time, he is about to fill his role alongside a young, aspiring core looking to make an impact.

An impact that was felt at practice.

In addition to Essengue, all of the major players got some shine and smiled along the way. Obviously, Caleb Wilson was doing everything there was to do. He took pull-up jumpers and attacked the rim. Matas Buzelis was energized as he got up. Dailyn Swain was having a good time.

Then, Jalen Smith capped off the practice between Team Black and Team Red with a game-winning shot.

It got INTENSE at the end of today's scrimmage 👀 https://t.co/KTDIifkM3B pic.twitter.com/g1l1beG4Ec

— Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) October 2, 2026

It seems the Bulls, looking to rebuild and start a new chapter, aren't settling for anything less. And that practice actually, for once, means something.

The Bulls begin the preseason against the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at the United Center at 7:00 pm CST/8:00 pm EST.

title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry Reveals Ayesha Curry Reaction to $20 Million Decision
description: The Golden State Warriors agreed to a discount contract for star guard Stephen Curry last week. But what did Ayesha Curry think? The post Warriors’ Stephen Curry Reveals Ayesha Curry Reaction to $20 Million Decision appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Certainly, Golden State Warriors point guard Stephen Curry has an understanding that the money he makes as an NBA player is well beyond the norm, not the kind of money his grandparents in the Carolinas got by on, and not even the kind of money that his dad, Dell Curry, had at his disposal when he was in the NBA from 1986-2002. So when it came down to figuring out how to handle his latest contract, an extension on his current deal that could have topped out at $137 million over two years, Curry had some perspective.

He did not take a whopping pay cut, but had handed back $20 million over two years to the Warriors, accepting a two-year deal worth $116 million, though with a player option in the second year that could allow him to push back to a max deal thereafter. While most of the focus on Curry's extension has been how the Warriors would react to having a chunk more free-agent money to spend next summer, one intrepid reporter wondered: What did Curry's wife, Ayesha Curry, have to say to giving up $20 million?

The question came ABC sports in the Bay Area: How did Ayesha Curry react to her husband's decision on his Warriors extension.

From the star guard: "That's why sometimes I realize like, this is not a real place, the NBA, because I can also say, people like, 'Oh, you stressed out about the decision,' and all that–the gratitude and understanding, the numbers we're talking about, and of course there's team valuations and the salary cap, max numbers and all. It goes back to my very first contract, the $11 million, the four for $44 million that I signed. You sign contracts based on information that you have and what you feel like is right.

"And you talk about Ayesha, my family, we, everybody's on the same page of understanding what I have in front of me in the controllables of we got playing good basketball, staying with the Golden State Warriors and trying to end this thing the right way."

This article was originally published on HEAVY

title: Dalton Knecht Emerges as Likely Lakers Roster Casualty
description: The Los Angeles Lakers may be gearing up to cut former first-round pick Dalton Knecht, according to a new report, as they shape the roster. The post Dalton Knecht Emerges as Likely Lakers Roster Casualty appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers may be gearing up to cut former first-round pick Dalton Knecht, according to a new report, as they shape the roster.

The Lakers currently have 16 players on the roster, and by the time the season rolls around, that number will need to be 15.

On the bright side for the Lakers, they have depth and a good roster-building choice, but the decision will be tricky.

Among the players on the chopping block is Knecht, who is expected to be the odd man out according to a report from Khobi Price of the California Post.

"Not a good sign for Knecht, whom multiple rival executives expect to be the odd man out as the Lakers look to trim their roster from 16 players on standard NBA deals to the league maximum of 15," Price wrote in his report.

Knecht was taken with the No. 17 overall pick back in the 2024 NBA Draft. However, midway through his rookie year, he was traded to the Hornets for center Mark Williams, but the trade was ultimately canceled.

Williams stayed with the Hornets, and Knecht returned to the Lakers, leading to an awkward reintegration period.

He struggled since then to look like the promising player that he once was.

Still, JJ Redick sees a player who is trying hard and wants to make the team and get minutes.

"First of all, he's been a pro," Redick said. "He's been in the gym. Like he has since Day 1, he has worked his butt off all offseason. And he's had a good three days of practice. So I don't think his approach changes. I know he's hungry to play and hungry to earn a spot in the rotation."

Knecht shot 37.6% from deep his rookie year, then 34.2% the following season. As a shooter, he needs to start shooting more efficiently.

If he can find his confidence and start creating offense again, Knecht could beat the odds and stay with the team.

He has a role on the wings, but he will need to take it.

title: Tony Finau, Maverick McNealy among stars headed home early from Bank of Utah Championship
description: Austin Smotherman leads the Bank of Utah Championship while notable players like Tony Finau and Maverick McNealy missed the weekend cut.
fullText:
It's a birdie-fest this week on the PGA Tour at the Bank of Utah Championship in Ivins, Utah.

Black Desert Resort, a Tom Weiskopf/Phil Smith design, has given up birdies by the bushels, especially to Austin Smotherman, who torched the course to the tune of 17-under 125 and the lead at the midway point of the second event of the FedEx Cup Fall portion of the schedule.

Friday's second round was suspended at 7:20 p.m. local due to darkness. It will resume Saturday morning at 9 a.m. local, with three players needing to complete their second rounds, including Alejandro Tosti and Jesper Svensson, who were 5 under and on the wrong side of the cutline by a shot through 34 holes. It took 6-under 136 to make the weekend out of the 120-man field.

Seamus Power made sure he was among them, tallying eight birdies on Friday, including at two of the last three holes to secure weekend work.

Past champion Matt McCarty two-putted from 91 feet for birdie at 18 to make it on the number. Brendon Todd shot 67 and made just his second cut in eight starts this season.

Joel Dahmen birdied the last two holes – from 25 feet and 9 feet – to shoot even-par 71 and earn a paycheck while Davis Thompson did him one better – three off the cut line with six holes to go, he birdied four holes on the front nine to get the job done.

Patrick Rodgers was straddling the cut line before making birdies on the last four holes to shoot 64 and make it with room to spare. Likewise, Jackson Koivun closed with three birdies in his final five holes to shoot 67 and make the cut on the number a week after his Presidents Cup debut.

He's not the youngest player to make the cut this week. Props to BYU sophomore and U.S. Walker Cupper Kihei Alina, who shot a pair of 67s to make the weekend. But not everyone booked a weekend tee time. Let's take a close look at some of the notables who went home early.

At least it will be a short drive home for Utah's favorite son. The Lehu resident missed his second straight cut and now has just one top-30 finish in his last 16 starts to show for it. Not good for a six-time Tour winner. An opening-round 70 that included a double bogey and two more bogeys dug him a hole and while he shot a bogey-free 68 on Friday, his putter held him back from going low and he missed the cut by one.

"I played really nicely today," Finau said. "Just a couple little things and a couple putts go my way — I feel like I hit really good putts and they just didn't go in. Looks like I'm going to probably just miss the weekend, but some positives as I move into next week."

Finau entered next week's Tour start in Japan. In his pre-tournament interview, he said he'll likely tee it up at the Vidanta Mexico Open, a tournament where he's a past champion.

McNealy is locked in the top 50 but given he makes his residence in nearby Las Vegas, he was apt to tee it up in southern Utah. McNealy (69-68) suffered from a poor putting week. He ranked 115th out of 118 players who completed 36 holes, losing nearly 4½ strokes on the short grass. It was just his third missed cut in 22 starts this season.

The veteran pro knows what it's all about battling the cut line, and he made a good fight, carding seven birdies on Friday but it wasn't enough. He found himself behind the proverbial 8-ball because he made a triple-bogey 7 at the first hole, his 10th of the day on Thursday. Glover struggled on the greens, ranking 106th in SG: putting.

Hardy and Davis were desperate to make a cut and it looked as if they had done enough only to fall to the wrong side of the cutline. Hardy, who entered the week at No. 193 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, made five back-nine birdies to get to 5 under. But he's still stuck at three made cuts in 13 starts.

Davis tried to overcome a triple-bogey at the par-5 seventh hole. He carded three birdies and no bogeys the rest of the way to shoot 70 but finished one shy of making the cut. He's 191st in the season-long standings with just 5 made cuts in 18 starts.

The reigning PGA Tour Rookie of the Year remains mired in a slump. He shot 71-69 to miss the cut for the sixth time in his last eight starts. The long-hitting South African got off to an inauspicious start when his opening tee shot Thursday flew into the black lava and he made triple bogey. It was the driver early but the putter throughout that let him down. Potgieter lost more than a stroke on the greens both rounds and ranked No. 106 in SG: putting through 36 holes.

The 39-year-old Swede made his first PGA Tour start since the 2024 American Express. He still hasn't made a cut since the 2023 Bermuda Championship after rounds of 71 and 75. Lingmerth was done in by two double bogeys on his first nine of the second round on Friday. But at least his chronic back pain that kept his sideline for two years has improved to the point that the former one-time Tour winner can chase his dreams again.

Adam Schupak is a Golfweek senior writer covering the PGA Tour.

title: Laney football crushes Topsail, rekindles fire after turbulent start
description: After a soul-crushing overtime loss last week, Laney football responded with a dominant win over Topsail in Week 7.
fullText:
There's been little normal about Laney football's first season under coach Coraey Houser.

A canceled opener, a flooded locker room and three games in the span of a week have been mixed into a 2026 season that hasn't always gone the way the Buccaneers hoped.

But on Friday, Oct. 2 in Hampstead, Laney finally got a chance to leave some of that frustration behind.

Fresh off a crushing overtime loss to Ashley in Week 6, the Bucs started fast and dominated all night, cruising to a 34-6 win over Topsail in Week 7 of the 2026 North Carolina high school football season.

"It brought a lot of anger out of us," Laney senior running back Jeremiah Brown said of the loss to Ashley. "We didn't execute the right way and that's why we had to lock in this week."

WEEK 7 SCORES North Carolina high school football scores, live updates for Week 7

Brown rushed for more than 170 yards and a touchdown as Laney (3-4, 2-1 Carolina Coast) delivered perhaps its most complete performance of an otherwise turbulent season.

The Bucs' opener was postponed twice because of weather before eventually being canceled. Flooding in the team's locker room created another headache, and a makeup game against Northside between Weeks 4 and 5 left Laney playing three times in eight days.

Through all of it, the Bucs have tried not to let the frustration consume them.

"I can't say it hasn't been a struggle, but it's been a fun struggle," Laney quarterback Joseph Stough said. "It's all about just keeping that brotherhood between us. I think that's what this win proved tonight."

That perspective starts with Houser.

The first-year coach remembers standing at midfield in Week 1 as his players learned for the second time that they wouldn't be playing that night. It was an early lesson in how quickly plans can unravel during a high school football season, and one Houser has tried to turn into something his players can carry with them.

"I tell them every day, the sun's still gonna shine tomorrow," Houser said. "It might not shine in Wilmington, North Carolina, but it's going to shine somewhere."

Friday, it felt a little brighter for the Buccaneers.

The win extended Laney's advantage in the all-time series against Topsail to 12-2, with the team still unbeaten in Hampstead.

More importantly, after everything that has made Houser's first season unpredictable, Laney looked like the team it hoped to become when the fall began.

"This is a huge win for us," Houser said. "This win kept us together. … This was a game we needed. It was a game we had to execute and do everything right."

description: The Braves are using the same strategy for the second game in a row.
fullText:

Sep 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Atlanta Braves starting pitcher Brent Suter (39) throws against the Miami Marlins in the first inning at loanDepot Park. Mandatory Credit: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Atlanta has not formally announced its Game 1 starter, but the team is expected to use a bullpen game with left-hander Brent Suter as a potential opener. The Braves used Ray Kerr as an opener in Thursday's series-clinching win over the Philadelphia Phillies, with Kerr ultimately throwing 3⅓ innings.

The unusual strategy is largely a product of Atlanta's pitching situation. Chris Sale, who started Game 1 against Philadelphia, was used in relief to close out the Wild Card Series and will not be available to start until at least Game 2 against Los Angeles. Tyler Mahle is also lined up no earlier than Game 3.

That leaves Grant Holmes, J.R. Ritchie and other bullpen options as possibilities for the opening game.

The Braves will be trying to navigate a difficult pitching situation against a Dodgers lineup that will enter the series rested after receiving a first-round bye. Los Angeles has several established starters available, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow among the options.

For Atlanta, the opener strategy could allow manager Walt Weiss to mix and match against the Dodgers rather than commit to one traditional starter for a lengthy outing.

Game 1 is scheduled for Saturday at 4 p.m. ET at Dodger Stadium, with the Braves looking to take an early advantage in the best-of-five NLDS.

title: USC Trojans lose starting wide receiver for season with knee injury
description: USC starting safety Corey Simms will miss the rest of the season with a knee injury. He started three games for the Trojans.
fullText:
The USC Trojans will be without starting wide receiver Corey Simms for the rest of the season after he suffered a knee injury, according to Matt Zenitz and Chris Hummer of CBS Sports.

Simms played USC's first four games of the season before missing last week's game against the Oregon Ducks. He made the first three starts os his career before his season came to an early end. The sophomore is fourth on the team with 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown.

He had the best game of his career against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, catching four passes for 72 yards and the first touchdown of his career. He played in all 13 games last year as a true freshman, but his biggest contributions were on special teams, with him catching just one pass for six yards.

His absence puts even more pressure on USC quarterback Jayden Maiava and the rest of the offense. Freshman wide receiver Trent Mosley, who has missed the past two games, was listed as doubtful on the Friday injury report ahead of this weekend's game against Washington. He has 13 receptions for 255 yards and a team-high four touchdown receptions.

USC (4-1, 1-1 Big Ten) is looking to bounce back from its 41-27 loss to Oregon on Saturday when they host the Washington Huskies (3-1, 0-1). The game is set to start at 4:30 p.m. PT and will air on NBC.

USC wide receiver Corey Simms is expected to miss the rest of the season due to a knee injury, sources tell me and @chris_hummer.

title: Paul Sullivan: Can White Sox keep succeeding in postseason without conventional rotation?
description: CLEVELAND — If you’re a baseball fan of a certain age, you’ve probably spent most of your life knowing some certainties about a pitching staff. The five best guys (or four if you’re really old) are the starters who will try to get you through the bulk of the game. The best reliever is the closer, who pitches the last inning or possibly part of the eighth if he’s dominant enough. The next-best ...
fullText:
CLEVELAND — If you're a baseball fan of a certain age, you've probably spent most of your life knowing some certainties about a pitching staff.

The five best guys (or four if you're really old) are the starters who will try to get you through the bulk of the game. The best reliever is the closer, who pitches the last inning or possibly part of the eighth if he's dominant enough. The next-best relievers — preferably one left-hander and one right-hander — are the setup men, the potential bridges from starter to closer.

And the pitcher who is least effective on the staff is the mop-up man, whose main function is keeping the better relievers from being overused.

For years managers used that basic blueprint, or something close to it, to get through the regular season. Then when the playoffs arrived, the best three or four starters went longer because the season was almost over and they could empty their bullets in the biggest games.

But baseball has changed, for better or worse, and now anything goes. Boston Red Sox ace Sonny Gray was removed in the fifth inning of a do-or-die wild-card game Wednesday, and Gray and his teammates grumbled about how the game got to this point.

Which brings us to the 2026 Chicago White Sox, who are trying to win with a "no-rotation" rotation.

Will Venable, the second-year White Sox manager, announced Friday that left-handed reliever Hagen Smith would start Game 1 of the American League Division Series against the Cleveland Guardians, serving as the opener Saturday, as he did in pitching three scoreless innings in Game 1 of the wild-card win in Houston.

It's no surprise. The Sox have used openers a league-leading 32 times this season, including Smith's outing Tuesday. If it ain't broke, don't fix it.

But does the no-rotation rotation have its limits, or can Venable's Sox keep succeeding in the postseason with a bullpen-first strategy?

Venable acknowledged Sean Burke could start Game 2 on Monday, as he did in a four-inning start in Game 2 against the Astros, in which starters Anthony Kay and Erick Fedde both pitched in relief. But other than Burke, it might be a guessing game from here on out.

Can Smith come back to start Game 3 at home Wednesday, giving him three starts in their first five playoff games? Who knows what's up Venable's sleeve?

"I think the way it's set up with these off days, we're going to leverage the arms that we want to leverage when we want to use them throughout these first couple," Venable said. "And if that means that one of the guys who we've been giving starts to throughout the season takes a bulk role in that, there's certainly potential for that. But I think you can expect us to mix and match and use our best arms in the most optimal way."

That suggests Smith and Grant Taylor can be the designated bookends of multiple games, with Jordan Hicks, David Sandlin and Sean Newcomb in the middle and Kay, Fedde and Davis Martin as the wild cards.

It's almost the polar-opposite approach that then-manager Ozzie Guillén employed in the 2005 postseason, when José Contreras, Mark Buehrle, Freddy Garcia and Jon Garland combined for a 2.84 ERA in 12 starts, leading the Sox on an 11-1 run to their World Series title.

In the five-game win over the Anaheim Angels in the AL Championship Series, the four starters had four straight complete games and combined for 44 1/3 of the 45 total innings, with Neal Cotts contributing the other two outs in the ninth inning of the Game 1 loss. The rest of the bullpen had a nice seat to watch the starters dealing.

"I don't know if you'll ever see that again," Sox catcher A.J. Pierzynski said afterward. "Managers just don't do that anymore. They don't have confidence to let guys go 120 pitches and throw nine innings."

In the World Series, advance scout Bryan Little and his crew gave Guillén and pitching coach Don Cooper a near-perfect report on strengths and weaknesses of the Astros hitters. Contreras and Buerhle both went seven innings in the first two wins at Sox Park, and Garland went seven in Game 3 in Houston before the Astros tied it off Dustin Hermanson in the eighth.

Guillén was forced to use his well-rested bullpen when the game went 14 innings but also used Orlando "El Duque" Hernández and Buehrle. After Geoff Blum's go-ahead home run in the 14th, Buehrle notched the infamous "buzzed save" by getting the final out after having a few beers in the clubhouse. "No more than three … I swear," he later said.

Buehrle wound up on a Wheaties box, but he didn't become a legend for his cereal-eating habits.

Game 4 was as old-school as it gets, with Garcia going seven shutout innings, Cliff Politte and Cotts getting the Sox through the eighth and Bobby Jenks closing out a 1-0 win to start the parade plans.

"That type of game is like the ones I watched for 162 games during the regular season," Guillén said in the celebratory clubhouse.

Venable's approach in the postseason also mirrors what he has done for much of the season.

General manager Chris Getz knew he didn't have a dominant rotation in spring training, and opening-day starter Shane Smith was quickly dispatched to Triple-A Charlotte after three starts. Martin, Burke, Kay and Fedde have been the mainstays, though Fedde, who signed at the start of spring training, had only 15 starts in his 33 games.

Taylor has evolved into the de facto closer but can go three innings if needed. He also was used as an opener in April. Seranthony Domínguez led the team 12 saves, even after being dispatched at the trade deadline.

Openers aren't a new concept. "Bullpenning" has been around for the last decade. Cubs manager Craig Counsell also used openers in last year's postseason.

But is it possible no team has been as unconventional as the '26 Sox in this particular run?

"It's possible," Getz said during the wild-card celebration. "We weren't trying to re-create the wheel. We were trying to optimize the group that we had. So much of (baseball) has relied on starting pitching. We would've liked to do that. But if we were trying to win games, we had to lean on the strength of the club, and we've done that."

The Sox's strategy has been criticized, especially when an opener puts the bulk pitcher in a hole. Guillén himself has said on the Chicago Sports Network he's not a fan of openers.

But if the Sox go all the way without a true rotation, the players may never have to buy a meal or drink in Chicago again. Or at least that's the adage.

"More often than not I'll just roll in and buy a drink or buy my dinner," Blum told me last week in Houston. "But every so often, if there is a hard-core Sox fan in the bar or in the restaurant, there will be a free drink that will show up once in a while."

"It still carries a little bit of weight," Blum said. "We're not quite the '85 Bears, but the '05 Sox do OK."

title: Plainville football stays unbeaten as Abarno and defense deliver dominant win over Tolland
description: Abarno accounts for five TDs as Plainville's defense shuts out Tolland in CCC battle of unbeatens.
fullText:
PLAINVILLE - Who's that up there with the Daniel Hands and Ansonias of the Connecticut high school football world? Right there at the top of the CIAC Class SS playoff rankings?

That would be Plainville, a spotless 4-0 after routing Tolland 40-0 Friday night in a CCC Tier 4 battle of unbeatens at Tinty Field.

What was supposed to be a showdown turned out to be a showcase instead, featuring a shutdown defense and one of the state's most accurate passers.

That would be Anthony Abarno. Plainville's senior quarterback completed 21 of 30 passes for 266 yards and four touchdowns. He also ran for a score as the Blue Devils steadily built leads of 7-0 after one quarter, 21-0 by the half, and 33-0 by the end of three.

Abarno connected twice on scoring passes with Chase Bouchard. They opened the game with a 16-yard strike and closed it with a 15-yard connection in the opening minute of the fourth quarter, which put the game on running time.

Abarno also found Christian Hairston from 31 yards out in the second quarter and Billy Putnam from 19 in the third.

Putnam, the kicker, went 5-for-5 on PATs and also booted a 31-yard field goal.

Plainville's defense, after allowing a 35-yard gain on the opening carry to Tolland scatback Jon Carlos Gonzalez, a 100-yard rusher in each of his first three games, lowered the boom and kept the Eagles off the board.

Led by senior linebacker Dylan Feltt, a fourth-year starter, the Blue Devils twice stopped Tolland on fourth downs just over midfield in the first half when the game was still tight.

The Plainville D also chalked up a safety in the third quarter, sacking Tolland QB Caleb Graham in the end zone, and recovered a pair of fumbles courtesy of linebackers Jose Gutierrez and Javin Arocho.

Friday marked both Homecoming and the home opener for Plainville, which kicked off with road wins at Lewis Mills (48-7), Joel Barlow (49-20) and Newington (21-6).

Tolland also came in at 3-0 and fresh from its most impressive win of the season to date, 37-8 over Bloomfield. It's been a remarkable turnaround season so far for the Eagles, who were 1-9 a year ago.

title: How Sean Durzi Came To Rangers Thanks To Vincent Trocheck
description: Sean Durzi didn’t wait long to make his mark with the New York Rangers. He scored a quick goal on Friday night against the Detroit Red Wings, and he was almost involved in a second before the first period ended — only a miniscule offside overruled it. Still, it was pretty fast proof in Durzi’s […] The post How Sean Durzi Came To Rangers Thanks To Vincent Trocheck appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Sean Durzi didn't wait long to make his mark with the New York Rangers.

He scored a quick goal on Friday night against the Detroit Red Wings, and he was almost involved in a second before the first period ended — only a miniscule offside overruled it.

Still, it was pretty fast proof in Durzi's Rangers tenure that he's a guy who can make an impact as a defenseman at both ends of the nice.

He's also a player, though, who has flown under the radar heading into a new season. The busy sports ecosystem in New York City can keep a blue-liner relatively unknown until he's actually out there doing things.

Durzi is here now, though, and getting himself noticed.

The Rangers have Vincent Trockeck to help for his arrival.

Durzi came to the Rangers in the Vincent Trocheck trade.

It was an exercise in patience for the Rangers, who had rumors swirling around Trocheck for months and months.

Even when New York traded away Artemi Panarin before the deadline, they opted to hold onto Trocheck. He was still under contract, and so they didn't need to move him yet.

But on July 1, the Rangers did trade Trocheck.

They sent him to the Utah Mammoth for Durzi as well as the prospect Cole Beaudoin and a 2027 third-round pick.

Durzi was coming off a season with five goals and 22 assists (27 points) in 60 games with the Mammoth in 2025-26.

Now, he's trying to do even better for the Rangers as part of a defensive group with a lot of talent.

Durzi is originally from Mississauga in Ontario, Canada.

He went on to play at the junior level in the OHL with the Owen Sound Attack.

The Toronto Maple Leafs drafted Durzi No. 52 overall (second round) in the 2018 NHL Draft.

He actually was a goalie when he first played hockey, but the story goes that his mom preferred he play defenseman, and so that's what he did.

The Maple Leafs traded Durzi before he got near the NHL, sending him to the Los Angeles Kings less than a year after he was drafted.

He played with the Kings through the 2022-23 season, then was traded to the Arizona Coyotes for a 2024 second-round pick.

Arizona moved to Utah, and Durzi was there until he was then sent to the Rangers. Now he's in the Big Apple hoping to make his mark.

title: Maryland women’s soccer crushed in 4-0 loss to Minnesota
description: The Terps remain goalless through six Big Ten games.
fullText:
Through the first 30 minutes of the second half, Maryland women's soccer held Minnesota to just three second-half shots.

Unfortunately for the Terps, all three ended up in the back of the net.

Minnesota's offense ran to perfection all night, and Maryland's lack of attacking firepower was no match. The Terps fell to the Golden Gophers, 4-0, for their largest margin of defeat this season.

Minnesota's first chance came in the ninth minute from an Ava Paolini foul that led to a dangerous free kick. Faith Luckey saved a shot from Ava Westlund, and on the ensuing corner kick, Westlund's header ricocheted just off the post. After some pandemonium in the box, Luckey once again punched the ball out of danger.

Just moments later, Luckey came through again for the Terps, denying Matigann Vixayvong after the midfielder made an incisive run. Seconds later, a shot from Ellen Neuharth required a diving stop from Luckey, who made another excellent save.

That would be the high point defensively of the night for Maryland.

In the 24th minute, Taylor Heimerl took the ball down the left side and fired a dangerous cross. Tenley Senden could not receive the ball as she fell in the box, got up and set up Vixayvong in open space.

On what was already the Golden Gophers' eighth shot in the game, Vixayvong refused to be denied again and slotted the ball past Luckey.

Minnesota's offense was relentless throughout the first half of play. The Golden Gophers fired 15 shots, tied for the most Maryland has allowed in a half all year.

Ava Westlund had five of those, coming mere inches from scoring an early goal, but Vixayvong's goal would be the only score of the first half.

After a dominant offensive first half, the Gophers' attack got even better in the second.

Minutes after Westlund stepped back on the field for the second half, she would get a breakthrough of her own.

After she received the ball just outside the box, Westlund fired a shot towards the top of the goal, and Luckey could not get a hand to it, doubling the Golden Gophers' lead.

Westlund's scoring wasn't done.

In the 55th minute, Caroline Birdsell slotted a picture-perfect pass right to Westlund's foot, who had just Luckey to beat. A poke past the goalkeeper was all Westlund needed to find the back of the net for the second time.

Just four minutes later, another beautiful pass into the box from Birdsell set up Katelyn Brigg, who took advantage to continue the onslaught.

Minnesota finished with 23 shots in the game and completely dominated on offense from start to finish.

For Maryland's offense, it was a different story.

The Terps had three shots in the first half, but there were signs of offensive potential. Both of Maryland's two shots on goal required great plays from Martin. However, the volume was not there to put real pressure on the Golden Gophers' defense.

The Terps' best chance after Minnesota's first goal came when Maryland attacked right back down the field with some offense of its own. Despite a great run, Peyton Bernard's shot would come up empty after a great save from Sarah Martin.

Ultimately, the lack of volume hindered any comeback efforts.

Maryland attempted zero shots until late in the second half, and opportunities were few and far between. The Terps held barely any possession in attacking possession, mostly being on their heels from a relentless assault from the Golden Gophers.

A late push accounted for all six of Maryland's second-half shots, but the game was well out of reach by the time the Terps started finding chances on attack.

As Minnesota scored goal after goal, the Terps could not find any way to answer.

The Golden Gophers dug holes. In nature, gophers are small burrowing animals. In soccer, the Golden Gophers found plenty of holes in the Terps defense that allowed Minnesota's attackers plenty of space to operate. Minnesota's attackers took advantage, scoring their most goals in a game in Big Ten play this season.

Dani Gichner will be missed. In the second minute of the game, Gichner went down with an injury and had to be helped off the field. Obviously, the defense did not hold up without her. If Gichner misses time, the Terps may struggle mightily in her absence.

Paige Foye might be Maryland's most important player. Foye was absent against Minnesota, serving the one-game suspension that comes with getting shown a red. The Terps collapsed without Foye against UCLA, and with her absent for a full game, the defense had its worst performance of the season. She may be a freshman, but the difference when Foye is on the field compared to when she is not is stark.

title: Hasbrouck Heights football stuns Butler to shake up NJIC playoff race
description: The Aviators delivered one of the program's biggest victories in recent memory Friday night in a key NJIC Meadowlands showdown in Bergen County.
fullText:
HASBROUCK HEIGHTS — Matt Samperi provided the spark. Nick Haines supplied the firepower. Together, they helped Hasbrouck Heights shake up the Northern New Jersey Interscholastic Conference playoff race.The Aviators, ranked No. 12 in the latest North Jersey Public Super 20, delivered one of the program's biggest victories in recent memory on Friday Oct. 2, knocking off two-time defending NJIC champion and No. 5-ranked Butler, 30-27 at Depken Field.

The victory not only snapped Butler's grip atop the conference, but also thrust Hasbrouck Heights squarely into the championship conversation when the NJIC playoffs get underway in two weeks.

Samperi ignited the Aviators with a series of momentum-changing plays on defense, while Haines accounted for key offensive production as Hasbrouck Heights overcame the Bulldogs in a back-and-forth battle that came down to the final minutes.

Samperi's tackle in the end zone for a safety early in the third quarter pulled Hasbrouck Heights within 14-8 and shifted the momentum. Haines then took over, scoring on a 13-yard touchdown run in the closing minutes of the third quarter before electrifying the home crowd with a 95-yard kickoff return touchdown early in the fourth, giving the Aviators the lead for good.

The win marked Heights' first victory over Butler since 2019 and improved the Aviators to 4-2, while the Bulldogs fell to 5-1.

title: Wisconsin women's hockey survives challenge with huge test at Ohio State next
description: The top-ranked Badgers got more of a test than they probably wanted, but they responded. Now they face rival Ohio State short-handed.
fullText:
MADISON – After three lopsided games and then one that stayed too close for too long, life is about to get that much more difficult for the Wisconsin women's hockey team.

The top-ranked Badgers, looking for their third straight NCAA title and 10th overall, wrapped up the pre-conference portion of their schedule Oct. 2 with a 4-1 comeback victory over Boston University at LaBahn Arena.

Next comes a road series Oct. 9-10 against archrival Ohio State in which Wisconsin will be without at least three important players.

"We'll think about that Sunday," coach Mark Johnson said. "It's been a busy couple of weeks.

"It's early in the process, and so a bunch of things are coming at us early on, and so how do you respond? Everything's been really positive in that aspect."

After a 7-0 Wisconsin victory in the home opener a night earlier, BU led more than half the second game and kept it tied for nearly 12 minutes more.

Terriers freshman Lo Lachapelle scored with five seconds left on a 5-minute power play 15:18 into the game. Badgers senior center Cassie Hall finally evened the score midway through the second, and her second goal of the game – one she thought Finley McCarthy actually tipped in – put UW on top. Junior forward Maggie Scannell had the first assist on both of Hall's goals.

Then Slovakian freshman forward Nela Lopušanová, who scored twice in the series opener, added her fourth goal as a Badger barely three minutes later. Laney Potter hit an empty net from long range with just over four minutes remaining, leaving UW at 4-0 and BU at 0-4.

"We had chances right off the start of the game, and I think it really tested us," Hall said. "In between the second and third period, we kind of settled down, played as a team. Not everyone can be the hero; [we] talked about that, and finally with patience we were able to put, what, three more in."

While the Badgers play the Buckeyes in a matchup of the past four NCAA title games, defenders Ava Murphy and Emma Venusio and forward Rosalie Tremblay will be in training camp with the Canadian national team.

Left wing Kelly Gorbatenko, the team's captain, left the game after being hit on the wrist by a puck and her status is unclear. Gorbatenko, a senior who has never missed a game as a Badger, did stay in the bench area after being hit.

Ohio State started its season on the road with of 2-1 victories over Penn State and a Friday-Saturday WCHA series at St. Thomas.

Wisconsin and Ohio State have combined to take the past seven NCAA championships with UW winning in 2019, '21, '23, '25 and '26, and they've played each other for the title the past four seasons.

In the post-COVID era, UW holds a 17-16-1 advantage in the series but has gone 4-8 in Columbus. Seven of the games in that span have gone beyond 60 minutes.

title: Will Bears beat the Jets? Our game picks and bold predictions
description: The Chicago Bears battle the New York Jets in Week 4 as Ben Johnson battles Aaron Glenn. Can the Bears improve to 3-1?
fullText:
The Chicago Bears (2-1) are gearing up for a Week 4 matchup against the New York Jets (1-2) on Sunday, where Ben Johnson and Aaron Glenn will face off for the first time since both left the Detroit Lions for head coaching jobs.

The Bears are coming off an impressive 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, where they once again dominated the trenches and made a statement with third-stringer Case Keenum under center amid quarterback injuries. Keenum orchestrated Ben Johnson's offense to perfection, completing 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and accounting for three total touchdowns. Meanwhile, Chicago's defense had an even better showing in Week 3, holding the Eagles to just seven points, forcing three turnovers and completely shutting them down in the second half.

Now, the focus shifts to a potenital trap game for Chicago, as the Jets have put up a fight against fellow NFC North squads Detroit and Green Bay, before both emerged victorious. Could the Bears be the first NFC North team to win convincingly against New York this season? Our Bears Wire staff certainly thinks so. Here's a look at their game predictions for Bears-Jets in Week 4:

Bold prediction: Bears record 3 takeaways again

The Bears proved they're a good football team with a statement win against the Eagles on Monday night, down their starting and backup quarterbacks. While the Jets aren't the Jets or miserable years past, this is a game that good football teams should win, so I'm expecting nothing less Sunday at Soldier Field. Obviously, the biggest question heading into this game is whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum will start at quarterback with Caleb Williams still sidelined. And, honestly, Keenum showed everyone last week that it doesn't really matter. Chicago can win with either Williams, Bagent or Keenum. As long as Ben Johnson is running the show, the Bears are one of the best in the NFL, and he'll have any QB ready to play.

Chicago's run game struggled early against Philadelphia last week, and it won't get any easier against one of the league's top run defenses in New York, which is allowing 87.3 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift was a surprise addition to Thursday's injury report with a knee injury, which is certainly worth monitoring, and Kyle Monangai could very well see an uptick in carries. That means Bagent or Keenum might once again have to carry this offense and attack downfield with this array of weapons.

The good -- and still shocking -- news is that the Bears defense has experienced a resurgence after allowing 37 points to the Panthers in Week 1. They're allowing an average 8.0 points per game in the last two contests, and they have an opportunity to continue that hot streak against a Jets team down top running back Breece Hall. Geno Smith is a solid quarterback, but if Chicago can do what they did last week against Jalen Hurts, it could result in another three-takeaway performance.

Bold prediction: Bears shut out Jets in first half

The New York Jets haven't beaten the Chicago Bears in the state of Illinois this millennium, and their first win sure as heck isn't coming with Ben Johnson at the helm. After three weeks, it's becoming clear that the Bears can be a powerhouse in the NFC, and it may not even matter who starts at quarterback. As of this writing, we still don't know whether Case Keenum will get another start with Caleb Williams on the mend or if Tyson Bagent will get the nod. While I'm leaving Bagent, I believe Johnson can carve up this New York defense with either player despite them allowing fewer than 200 total yards in their first couple of games.

These aren't the same old Jets from last year, as they've shown to be quite competitive to start the year. But they're banged up at multiple positions, particularly on offense, and are limited by the effectiveness of Aaron Glenn when it comes to in-game situations. With Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell likely out, Geno Smith will have a tougher time keeping pace with his early-season success. Especially if Olu Fashanu suddenly can't block anyone after allowing three sacks last week against the Detroit Lions.

The Bears are hitting their stride on both offense and defense, and unless another rainstorm engulfs Soldier Field, they will have no trouble taking care of business to start 3-1 for the first time since 2020.

Bold prediction: Dillon Thieneman scores first career TD

This game is tailor-made for the Chicago Bears to leave their impact across the league with Ben Johnson, once again showcasing his offensive excellence as a head coach. The New York Jets are coming in banged up, missing three of their top offensive players, so the defense should have a relatively smoother time in making lifetime on quarterback Geno Smith.

Dillon Thieneman excelled in last week's win over Philadelphia, and I believe the Bears playing at home will create multiple opportunities for the rookie to get his first career touchdown on a takeaway. I will add one more bold prediction, both Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum make appearances in this game. Ben Johnson loves to play to the crowd, and they will be roaring at home with a favorable matchup against the Jets.

Bold prediction: The Bears will run their offense even better this week with a backup QB than last week

The Chicago Bears have one of the best head coaches in the NFL, who also happens to be an elite playcaller. This is his chance to show it again as they face off against the New York Jets. He will have a backup QB under center again, but it shouldn't matter based on the scheming ability of the coach.

The Jets are not a great team, but they have given some scares to NFC North teams so far this year. The Bears will have to come ready to play if they want to make this a game in which they don't feel much pressure.

There is tape out there now to study on what Keenum looks like in his current form with his current team, so that's something for the Bears to think about. Even still, the talent up and down the field and on the sideline should allow them to pull away in the end.

Bold prediction: Chicago will sack Geno Smith at least five times

The New York Jets are not as bad as they have been in previous seasons. They really should have beaten the Green Bay Packers and nearly escaped Week 3 with a win against the Detroit Lions, so they will be competitive in this game as well, at least in the first half. New York only has one turnover in the first three games, so the Bears cannot rely on takeaways on defense to win.

Instead, they need to shut down Geno Smith and the passing attack. New York's running game has struggled and they will most likely be playing without star running back Breece Hall. If the Bears can prevent Smith from finding success against Chicago's defense in the passing game, it will be a long day for the Jets.

Chicago also needs to get pressure on Smith. In the past two games, he has been sacked nine times. The Bears only have seven sacks all year. However, they have the talent to get in the backfield and create havoc. Montez Sweat will have at least one of Chicago's sacks in this game.

Bold prediction: A Bears running back crosses the 100-yard threshold.

The Bears showed a lot against the Eagles on Monday night. They proved they can hang without Caleb Williams at the helm, and their defense continues to prove that they're better than what we saw in Week 1. While the Jets are a much better team than we've come to expect, this is also a matchup that should lean heavily in favor of the Bears if things come together like they did in Week 3.

The run game is what I'm watching. Each of D'Andre Swift & Kyle Monangai have struggled to gain traction since they each exploded back in Week 1. While the Jets have allowed one of the fewest yardage totals on the ground, they're closer to the middle of the pack in yards allowed per rush. Given how crucial it is to Ben Johnson's gameplan, I think that there will be a renewed focus on the ground game to the point where one of Swift (assuming he plays) or Monangai leaves a big impact on the stat sheet.

With the Jets facing a couple of injuries on the offensive side, I think the Bears' defense will continue gaining confidence despite some of their logistical shortcomings. Multiple turnovers again isn't entirely out of the question, and against one of the lower scoring teams in the league, it's completely possible the Jets don't touch the end zone before it's all done on Sunday.

title: Kyle Busch Celebration Of Life Event Details For Charlotte Motor Speedway
description: Join the NASCAR community on October 9 for the Kyle Busch Celebration of Life. Details on the free event at Charlotte Motor Speedway are now available.
fullText:
The NASCAR community will gather at Charlotte Motor Speedway on Friday, October 9, for a public Celebration of Life. This special event honors the life and legacy of Kyle Busch. The ceremony is free and open to everyone.

The event takes place at 8pm EST at the start/finish line in Concord, North Carolina. According to Motorsport.com NASCAR Cup, the ceremony will follow the Truck Series race. This is a huge moment for the sport. Busch was a massive talent. He won 234 races across three national divisions and earned two NASCAR Cup Series championships. He died suddenly on May 21 at the age of 41.

You do not need a ticket to join this tribute. The event is free to attend, and the track is offering free parking as well. If you already have a ticket for the Truck Series race, you can stay in your seat or move closer to the start/finish line. If you do not have a truck race ticket, you can still enter the track through Gates 4 and 5A. You just have to wait until the truck race ends to get in.

The timing might shift slightly because the ceremony starts right after the race. FOX SPORTS 1 will broadcast the event at 8pm EST, though this depends on when the Truck race finishes. I always tell people to check the schedule close to the date. Race delays happen, and you do not want to miss the start of the tributes.

This event will be a heavy night for racing fans. Many people close to Busch will speak. His wife, Samantha Busch, will be on stage. She is also a co-founder of their Bundle of Joy Fund. His brother, Kurt Busch, will also share memories. Kurt is a 2004 NASCAR Cup Series champion and a Daytona 500 winner. It will be powerful to hear from family members who knew him best.

The list of guest speakers includes several big names from the garage. NASCAR Cup, speakers will include:

Joe Gibbs, the owner of Joe Gibbs Racing where Busch won 56 of his 63 Cup wins.

Kyle Larson, a two-time Cup champion and current points leader.

Christopher Bell, a driver for Joe Gibbs Racing.

Daniel Suárez, a driver for Spire Motorsports.

Noah Gragson, a driver for Front Row Motorsports.

Austin Dillon, who was Busch's teammate at Richard Childress Racing until his death.

The night will also feature more than just speeches. There will be a full drone show and video tributes. The track will even display a curated collection of Busch's race cars and trophies. It is a massive way to show respect for a driver who changed the game.

The ceremony will not end with just the tributes. A post-ceremony concert by country star Cole Swindell is planned. It is a way to bring the community together after a very emotional program.

title: ArXiv imposes rate limit on paper submissions to stem the AI slop tide
description: Two a month per submitter, starting now, and you can thank science slop for the change
fullText:
Two a month per submitter, starting now, and you can thank science slop for the change

arXiv, the preprint paper repository, is seeing so many low-quality submissions, with AI tools helping drive the surge, that it has imposed a hard limit of two new submissions per month per submitter, regardless of whether they were produced solely by humans or with help from AI tools.

After becoming an independent nonprofit over the summer following 25 years under Cornell University’s stewardship, arXiv continued to rely on a “practical limit” in place that gave moderators the ability to determine whether someone was submitting too many papers. Like everything good and pure in this world, AI has ruined that, too, necessitating some strict new limits.

“arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time,” arXiv community engagement manager Kat Boboris wrote in a Thursday announcement of the change, which was effective immediately. According to an arXiv spokesperson, an active paper is one that has been submitted, is under consideration and review, but not yet published on the site.

It’s worth noting that large institutions whose projects involve multiple researchers are unlikely to see a significant impact on their submissions - this limit is per submitter, the announcement explains, so a research paper with multiple authors only counts toward the submission rate of the individual who files it. Rejected papers count toward that monthly total.

If that sounds like some strict limitation - it is, but it’s necessary, based on arXiv’s numbers.

In September alone, arXiv said that it had received 40,363 submissions. The same month 10 years ago saw it receive just 9,869 submissions; two years ago that number was 20,569. Submissions have increased 309 percent in the past decade, in other words - and doubled in the past two years alone.

Unsurprisingly, many of the submissions that arXiv has been receiving of late don’t meet its requirements for AI-assisted work, which call for significant use of generative AI tools to be disclosed, for those tools to be used in support of research, and for the resulting work to meet arXiv’s standards for scholarly interest and advancement of the field.

“Many of the submissions that arXiv is now receiving do not satisfy these requirements,” Boboris said, describing many recent submissions as “thin” and “narrow in scope,” and noting an uptick in papers that break a single work up over multiple smaller papers.

“A relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time,” arXiv editorial advisory council chair Thomas Dietterich said. “This is unfair to authors who continue to submit quality papers — their papers can be delayed for days or weeks as a result.”

It’s unfortunate it’s come to this, but the slop sluice is wide open and flooding the channels of academia. arXiv, as a non-profit with volunteer moderators, simply can’t afford to keep combing through the slop pits.

The change may not be permanent, however. arXiv notes in the announcement that the new monthly submission cap is a stopgap measure meant to stem the tide while the organization figures out what new best practices for submissions should look like, while its separate limit of three active submissions has been in place since 2024.

“arXiv will be monitoring the impact of this change on our submissions rates and moderation load to evaluate its overall effectiveness and impact on researchers and will make further changes as needed,” a spokesperson explained.

In the meantime, arXiv is begging everyone to be purposeful in their submissions.

“arXiv would ask researchers to prioritize their submissions and consider submitting papers that reflect the full scope of their work rather than multiple incremental papers,” the arXiv representative said.  ®
